hindi: अब इसके बाद हम गर्भव्यापद यानी गर्भ की विपत्तियों का, शारीर यानी शरीर सम्बन्धी का, व्याख्यान करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall explain garbhavyāpad (mishaps of the garbha, i.e. of the embryo or pregnancy), the śārīra (that which relates to the body).
notes: Opening formula of the chapter. Both garbhavyāpadam and śārīram are accusative; śārīra is probably the name of the sthāna (Śārīrasthāna), but the line itself only says 'relating to the body', so it is rendered literally. Modern equivalent of garbhavyāpad: complications or mishaps of pregnancy (probable).

words.gloss: come about / attained; garbha (embryo); pregnant (āpannagarbhā, lit. 'one whose garbha has come about')

hindi: यदि गर्भवती स्त्री, यानी जिसे गर्भ प्राप्त हुआ है, परिहार्य यानी त्यागने योग्य का सेवन करे।
english: If a woman who is pregnant (āpannagarbhā, lit. 'one whose garbha has come about') should indulge in avoidable (ones),

text_flags.why: possible: ṇi + ā-seveta should give ṇyāseveta with long ā; the print has short a (ṇyaseveta)

notes: Conditional clause; the main clause begins in the next units. 'parihāryāṇi' is neuter plural with no noun stated, so '(ones)' is used: the things to be avoided in pregnancy are not named here. The verb is read as ā-√sev 'indulge in' on the correction in text_flags; if the short a is right, no other verb form fits well.

words.gloss: of whom, whose (printed yasyā by regular sandhi before b-)
basti (urinary bladder region; standard); flank, side; hip, pelvis; yoni (vagina; standard); mouth, opening
puṣpa ('flower'; idiom for menstrual-type bleeding, probable); sight, appearance

hindi: उसमें जिस स्त्री के बस्ति यानी मूत्राशय के क्षेत्र, पार्श्व, श्रोणि और योनि के मुख में शूल यानी पीड़ा हो, या पुष्प यानी सम्भवतः रज का स्राव दिखाई दे,
english: In that case, in her for whom there should be pain in the basti (bladder region), the flanks, the hips and the mouth of the yoni (vaginal opening), or the appearance of puṣpa (the 'flower': an idiom for bleeding, probably menstrual-type bleeding),
notes: The sentence continues in unit 4 ('tām ... upācaret'). In 'basti-pārśva-śroṇi-yoni-mukheṣu' it is not certain whether 'mukha' belongs only to yoni (read here: 'mouth of the yoni') or to the whole list ('at the openings of ...'). Puṣpa-darśana is tagged probable as bleeding in pregnancy; the text itself says only 'sight of the flower'.
lines_deva: तत्र यस्या बस्तिपार्श्वश्रोणियोनिमुखेषु शूलं पुष्पदर्शनं वा स्यात्
lines_iast: tatra yasyā bastipārśvaśroṇiyonimukheṣu śūlaṃ puṣpadarśanaṃ vā syāt

cool; plaster, paste applied; sprinkling, pouring; and so on

hindi: उस स्त्री का, जो कोमल सतह वाले शीतल बिछावन की शय्या पर स्थित हो और जिसका सिर थोड़ा झुका हुआ हो, शीतल प्रदेह यानी लेप, परिषेक यानी सींचने आदि से उपचार करे।
english: Her, staying on a bed with a soft-surfaced, cool spread and with the head slightly lowered, one should treat with cool pradeha (plasters), pariṣeka (sprinklings) and the like.

text_flags.why: possible: 'mukha' read as 'face, surface' of the bedding; 'sukha' (comfortable) is a possible alternative reading, but the print gives a workable sense, so it is kept

notes: Main clause of the sentence begun in unit 3. 'mukha' is taken as 'surface, face' of the cool spread (as printed); 'sukha' (comfortable) would also suit. Uncertain how the first compound should be grouped; the translation takes it as bedding that is soft-surfaced and cool.

hindi: वह इस प्रकार है।
english: That is as follows.
notes: Introduces the list of measures that follows (units 6 onward).

words.gram: tat-puruṣa (sahasra 'thousand times' + dhauta), n. inst. sg.

hindi: हज़ार बार धोए हुए सर्पि यानी घी से नाभि के नीचे चारों ओर लेप करे।
english: With ghee (sarpis) washed a thousand times, one should smear (the area) all round below the navel.
notes: Two words are run together in print (sahasradhautena sarpiṣā). The avagraha in sarpiṣā'dho is an orthographic mark in the print (ā + a would simply give ā); adhaḥ is read as a word on its own with the ablative nābheḥ, as in the glossary's note on ūrdhvam + ablative. The object (the area) is not stated. 'Washed a thousand times ghee' is taken literally; the text does not say what the washing is done with.

hindi: मधुक यानी मुलेठी के साथ घी में, जो बहुत ठण्डा हो, पिचु यानी रुई का फाहा भिगोकर योनि के पास रखे।
english: Having soaked a picu (a pad or wad of cotton) in madhuka-ghee (madhuka: licorice) that is very cool, one should place (it) near the yoni.
notes: Madhuka is identified as licorice (standard); madhūka (Madhuca) is a different drug, but madhuka here is the usual licorice. 'madhuka-sarpiṣā' could also be read 'madhuka and ghee' (dvandva); the translation takes it as one thing, madhuka-ghee, without saying how it is made. 'picu' is a wad or pad, often of cotton. The object of 'sthāpayet' is the soaked picu.

words.gloss: nyagrodha (banyan, Ficus benghalensis; standard); and so on; decoction

hindi: गाय के दूध से, मधुक के जल से, अथवा न्यग्रोध यानी बरगद आदि के काढ़े से सींचे।
english: One should sprinkle (her) with cow's milk, with madhuka-water, or with a decoction of nyagrodha (banyan) and the others.

text_flags.why: possible: madhuka + ambu should give madhukāmbu with long ā; the print has short a

notes: Here kaṣāya in a sprinkling liquid is taken as 'decoction'. 'Nyagrodha and the others' is the nyagrodhādi group, but the text only says 'nyagrodha and so on'. The causative pariṣecayet is rendered simply as 'should sprinkle'. The object (her / the area) is not stated.

hindi: और योनि में तेलों को रखवाए, जिनका विशेषण परिपीततत्वरसानि अस्पष्ट है; अनुमानित पाठ पर ये ऐसे तेल हैं जिन्होंने किसी अस्पष्ट द्रव्य के रसों को भली भाँति सोख लिया है। अथवा उसके शृंग के साथ पकाए हुए दूध-घी का पिचु यानी फाहा।
english: And one should have oils (tailāni) placed in the yoni; the compound describing them, paripītatatvarasāni, is unclear, and on a conjectural reading they are oils that have thoroughly absorbed (paripīta) the juices (rasa) of an unclear substance. Or a picu (wad) of the milk-and-ghee cooked with its śṛṅga.

text_flags.why: possible and uncertain: 'tatva' is not a word; perhaps 'tat-tvak' (the bark of those, i.e. of the preceding trees), so 'oils that have absorbed the bark-juices of those'. Not adopted as firm.

notes: [02.04.9] Damaged or corrupt compound: kept unsplit and marked unclear. The words 'tailāni' and 'yonau' are run together in print. No firm sense for the middle of the compound; do not rely on the conjectural reading. [02.04.10] Elliptical: the verb (placing the wad, as in unit 7) is carried from the preceding units and not supplied. 'tat' is taken to point back to the nyagrodha-group of unit 8; 'śṛṅga' means 'horn' and in unit 19 'nyagrodha-śṛṅga' stands for tender shoots, so 'shoot' is probable here, not certain. 'kṣīrasarpis' is milk and ghee together.

words.gram: pres. part. ati-√sru, m./n. loc. sg.

hindi: रक्त के बहुत बहने पर तो उसी में से अक्ष की मात्रा खिलाए।
english: But when the blood flows too much, one should make (her) take, from that very (one), a measure of an akṣa.
notes: 'tataḥ eva' (from that very) points back to the milk-and-ghee of unit 10; the sense is the same as the book's 'from that'. akṣa, picu and karṣa are synonyms of one weight (about 10 g in the standard reckoning); stated once here. The printed 'tata eva' is regular sandhi of tataḥ + eva.

lines_iast: atisravati tu rakte tata evākṣamātraṃ prāśayet

hindi: अथवा केवल दूध-घी में से ही।
english: Or from the milk-and-ghee alone.
notes: Elliptical: the measure and the verb (to give) are carried from unit 11 and not supplied. 'kevalāt' contrasts with the milk-ghee cooked with 'tat-śṛṅga' of unit 10, i.e. the plain one.

words.gloss: padma (lotus, Nelumbo nucifera; standard); utpala (water lily, Nymphaea; probable); kumuda (white water lily, Nymphaea; probable); kiñjalka (filaments, stamens)
gairika (red ochre; standard); sarjarasa (resin of sarja, Shorea robusta, sal; probable); rasāñjana (extract of Berberis, rasaut; probable); powder

hindi: और पद्म यानी कमल, उत्पल यानी सम्भवतः नीला कमल और कुमुद यानी सम्भवतः श्वेत कुमुदिनी के केसर को, शहद और शर्करा यानी चीनी के साथ चटाए। अथवा धातकी यानी धाय, गैरिक यानी गेरू, सर्जरस यानी सम्भवतः साल की राल और रसाञ्जन यानी सम्भवतः रसौत का चूर्ण, शहद के साथ।
english: And one should make (her) lick the filaments (kiñjalka) of padma (lotus), utpala (probably a water lily) and kumuda (probably the white water lily), together with honey and sugar (śarkarā). Or a powder of dhātakī (woodfordia flowers), gairika (red ochre), sarjarasa (probably sal resin) and rasāñjana (probably barberry extract), with honey.

text_flags.why: possible: print leaves a space after dhātakī, but the singular 'cūrṇam' (powder) suggests dhātakī is a member of the same powder; read so

notes: [02.04.13] It is assumed that kiñjalka belongs to all three flowers; the compound alone would also allow 'padma, utpala, and the kiñjalka of kumuda'. Identifications: padma = Nelumbo nucifera (standard); utpala = Nymphaea species such as N. nouchali (probable); kumuda = white Nymphaea (probable). [02.04.14] Elliptical: the verb (lehayet) is carried from unit 13. Because of the space after dhātakī, a second reading is 'dhātakī, or a powder of gairika, sarjarasa and rasāñjana'; the first is taken. Sarjarasa could also be a resin from other trees; rasāñjana is the extract of dāruharidrā (Berberis), probable.

words.gloss: nyagrodha (banyan); and so on; bark; tender shoot; paste (kalka)

hindi: अथवा न्यग्रोध आदि की छाल और कोंपल का कल्क यानी लुगदी।
english: Or a paste (kalka) of the bark and the tender shoots (pravāla) of nyagrodha and the others.
notes: Elliptical: the verb is carried from the preceding units (how the paste is used is not stated). Words are run together in print (kalkaṃ vā). 'nyagrodha and the others' as in unit 8.

words.gloss: hare; of the eṇa antelope; deer; blood

hindi: अथवा खरगोश, सम्भवतः एण मृग और हिरण के रक्त को शहद के साथ पिलाए।
english: Or one should make (her) drink the blood of the hare, (probably) of the eṇa antelope and of the deer, with honey.

text_flags.why: possible: 'auṇa' is not a known word; śaśa + eṇa (the eṇa antelope) gives śaśaiṇa, which fits the animal list; the au/ai difference is a likely print error

notes: The reading 'eṇa' (śaśa + eṇa gives śaśaiṇa) is a conjecture, so the antelope is hedged ('probably'). Even without it the unit reads 'blood of the hare ... deer'.

words.gloss: vṛddhi (one of the aṣṭavarga drugs, Habenaria intermedia; disputed); vidārī (Pueraria tuberosa; probable); jīvantī (Leptadenia reticulata; standard)

hindi: अथवा वृद्धि यानी अष्टवर्ग की वृद्धि नामक औषधि जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, विदारी यानी सम्भवतः विदारीकन्द और जीवन्ती यानी डोडी, दूध के साथ।
english: Or vṛddhi (identity disputed), vidārī (probably Indian kudzu) and jīvantī (Leptadenia reticulata, a milky climber; standard), with milk.
notes: Elliptical: the verb (pāyayet) is carried from unit 16. The printed 'jīvantīr' is jīvantīḥ with r before v. Vṛddhi is usually taken as a drug of the aṣṭavarga (Habenaria intermedia) but this is disputed; vidārī may also be Ipomoea digitata (probable: Pueraria tuberosa).

words.gloss: candana (sandalwood, Santalum album; standard); and so on

hindi: नीलोत्पल यानी नीला कमल, सिता यानी मिश्री, अस्पष्ट पाठ पकलोष्ट, चन्दन आदि; अथवा तण्डुलाम्बु यानी चावल का पानी; अथवा अस्पष्ट पाठ सरसान्यसरेण।
english: Nīlotpala (blue water lily), sitā (crystal sugar), pakloṣṭa [unclear], sandalwood (candana) and the like; or taṇḍulāmbu (rice-water); or sarasānyasareṇa [unclear].

text_flags.why: possible and uncertain: 'pakloṣṭa' is not a word; 'pakva-loṣṭa' (baked clod) is a guess only

notes: Two printed forms (pakloṣṭa inside the first compound; the whole of sarasānyasareṇa) are not restorable and are left unsplit and marked unclear, with nothing built on them. The unit appears to continue the list of unit 17, with the verb carried from unit 16 and not supplied. 'sitā' is taken as sugar; it can also mean 'white' (something). 'candanādi' = 'sandalwood and so on'.

words.gloss: śālūka (edible rhizome of a water lily; probable)

hindi: गन्ध, प्रियंगु यानी सम्भवतः फूलप्रियंगु, काला उत्पल, शालूक यानी सम्भवतः जलकमल का कन्द, उदुम्बर यानी गूलर के कच्चे फल और न्यग्रोध यानी बरगद के अंकुर, अथवा बकरी के दूध से।
english: Gandha, priyaṅgu (probably Callicarpa macrophylla), dark utpala, śālūka (probably the edible rhizome of a water lily), the unripe fruits of udumbara (cluster fig) and the shoots of nyagrodha; or with goat's milk.

text_flags.why: possible: 'ungrodha' is not a word; 'ḍu-nyagrodha' (nya read as ṅ) fits the list; the dental d for ḍ is also a print slip

notes: One long compound with 'vā ājena payasā' (the 'vā''jena' mark is vā + ājena). Elliptical: the verb (pāyayet) is carried. Groupings are uncertain: 'gandha-priyaṅgu' may be one name; 'asita-utpala' could be 'asita' and 'utpala' separately; 'udumbara-śalāḍu' = unripe fruit of udumbara is assumed. The goat's milk is the vehicle (ājena payasā).

words.gloss: drākṣā (grape or raisin, Vitis vinifera); standard
ananta ('endless'; perhaps the drug anantā; identity disputed)

hindi: अथवा कसेरुक यानी सम्भवतः कसेरू, कमलनाल, सिंघाड़ा, गम्भारी, फालसा, द्राक्षा यानी मुनक्का, सारिवा यानी अनन्तमूल, अस्पष्ट अक्षर, पुण्डरीक यानी अनुमानित पाठ पर, सम्भवतः श्वेत कमल, अनन्त यानी पहचान विवादित द्रव्य, उत्पल, कन्द और बीज के काढ़े से, जो शर्करा और शहद से मीठा हो।
english: Or with a decoction of kaseruka (probably Scirpus grossus), lotus stalk (mṛṇāla), śṛṅgāṭaka (water chestnut), kāśmarya (Gmelina arborea), parūṣaka (phalsa, Grewia asiatica), drākṣā (grape or raisin), sārivā (Hemidesmus indicus), [unclear syllable ma], puṇḍarīka (on a conjectural reading; probably the white lotus), ananta (identity disputed), utpala, tuber(s) (kanda) and seed(s) (bīja), sweet with sugar and honey.

text_flags.why: possible: kvātha (decoction) written without v, as in unit 34
possible: 'proṃḍarīka' is puṇḍarīka (pu printed as pro); the syllable 'ma' after sārivā has no clear sense

notes: Long list of drugs for a decoction (kvātha). Scope of 'kanda-bīja' is not certain: it may belong to utpala and puṇḍarīka only ('tubers and seeds of ...'), or be list items; the translation lists them plainly. Only one syllable (ma) is unclear and it is marked, not translated. Ananta may be a name of sārivā or a separate drug; here it is left as disputed. Word 'kaseruka' = kaśeruka (Scirpus grossus; probable).

words.gloss: śāli (winter rice, Oryza sativa; standard); flour, ground paste

hindi: शालि का पिसा हुआ चूर्ण, अथवा जीवनीय के साथ उबाला हुआ दूध।
english: Ground śāli (rice) flour; or milk boiled with the jīvanīya (group).
notes: Ambiguous: piṣṭam, śṛtam and kṣīram all agree (neuter), so it may be one noun 'milk (kṣīra) [made with] śāli flour or boiled with jīvanīya'. The literal two-item reading is given. The verb is carried from the earlier units and not supplied. 'jīvanīya' is the standard name of a drug group; its members are not named here. The jīvanīya group is, in the classical (Caraka) list, ten drugs: jīvaka, ṛṣabhaka, medā, mahāmedā, kākolī, kṣīrakākolī, mudgaparṇī, māṣaparṇī, jīvantī, madhuka (standard for the group name; this line does not name the members, and several of them are themselves disputed).

kākolī (one of the aṣṭavarga drugs; identity disputed)

words.gloss: cool; vīrya (potency); jāṅgala (dry-land game, wild animals of arid country); broth, juice

hindi: और बला यानी बरियार, अतिबला यानी सम्भवतः कंघी, शालि, षष्टिक यानी साठी चावल, अनुमानित पाठ पर ईख की जड़ और काकोली, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, से अनुमानित पाठ पर उबाले हुए दूध के साथ और शहद व शर्करा के साथ, बहुत ठण्डा लाल शालि का भात खिलाए, अथवा शीतवीर्य यानी शीतल शक्ति वाले जाङ्गल यानी शुष्क प्रदेश के वन्य पशुओं के रस से।
english: And one should feed red śāli rice-meal (odana), very cool, with milk boiled (on a conjectural reading) with balā (Sida cordifolia), atibalā (probably Abutilon indicum), śāli, ṣaṣṭika (sixty-day rice), sugarcane root (on a conjectural reading) and kākolī (identity disputed), together with honey and sugar; or with the broth of jāṅgala (dry-land game) that is cool in vīrya (potency).

text_flags.why: possible: 'keśu' for 'kṣu' (ṣaṣṭika + ikṣu-mūla gives ṣaṣṭikekṣumūla; kṣ/ś confusion); 'bhṛtena' for 'śṛtena' (bha/śa and ṛ forms similar; milk is 'boiled with' drugs in units 21, 25, 28)

notes: Two conjectural corrections are adopted in the translation and marked there (ikṣu, śṛta). 'keśu' = kṣu is not certain; 'ikṣu-mūla' could also be two items (ikṣu, mūla). 'bhṛta' could mean 'filled / prepared'. Structure: rice meal fed with milk boiled with the drugs, or with game broth. 'jāṅgala' is translated 'dry-land game' (standard meaning: animals of arid country, whose broth is meant). Hindi 'अनुमानित पाठ पर' marks the conjectures.

lines_iast: balā'tibalāśāliṣaṣṭikeśumūlakākolībhṛtena ca payasā samadhuśarkareṇa raktaśālyodanaṃ suśītaṃ bhojayecchītavīryajāṃgalarasena vā

hindi: और रक्तपित्त यानी रक्त बहने वाले रोग की क्रियाओं का प्रयोग करे, शोधन को छोड़कर।
english: And one should apply the treatments (kriyā) of raktapitta (a bleeding disorder, lit. 'blood-pitta'), excluding the cleansing (śodhana) ones.
notes: Two words are run together in print (varjyāḥ prayuñjīta). Raktapitta: a disorder with bleeding from the body openings; the modern near-equivalent is a haemorrhagic or bleeding disorder (probable). Śodhana = cleansing procedures such as emesis and purgation. 'varjyāḥ' agrees with kriyāḥ.

hindi: और सौम्य, मन के अनुकूल कथाएँ।
english: And gentle (saumya) talks that are agreeable to the mind.
notes: Elliptical: the verb (prayuñjīta, 'should use') is carried from unit 23 and not supplied. 'saumya' = gentle, also 'cooling' (of the moon).

words.gloss: madhuka (licorice); payasyā (identity disputed; usually kṣīravidārī); asura-dāru (drug name, unidentified)

hindi: परन्तु जिसमें रक्त दिखाई न दिया हो उसे मधुक, पयस्या, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, और असुरदारु नामक अज्ञात द्रव्य के साथ पकाया हुआ दूध पिलाए।
english: But for her in whom blood has not been seen, one should make (her) drink milk cooked with madhuka, payasyā (identity disputed) and asura-dāru (a drug name, unidentified).
notes: 'a-dṛṣṭa-śoṇitā' = one in whom blood has not been seen, i.e. pain without a visible discharge. Payasyā is disputed (kṣīravidārī, Pueraria tuberosa var., or others). 'asura-dāru' is not identified; do not equate it with deva-dāru (devadāru, Cedrus deodara); 'amara-dāru' would be a different reading, not adopted. The dāru member may also be read as a separate word 'dāru'.
lines_deva: अदृष्टशोणितां तु मधुकपयस्यासुरदारुभिः सिद्धं पयः पाययेत्
lines_iast: adṛṣṭaśoṇitāṃ tu madhukapayasyāsuradārubhiḥ siddhaṃ payaḥ pāyayet

hindi: अथवा ताम्रवल्ली, अश्मन्तक, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है और जिसे प्रायः आपटा माना जाता है, शतावरी और पयस्याओं के साथ।
english: Or with tāmravallī (unidentified), aśmantaka (identity disputed; usually Bauhinia racemosa), śatāvarī (asparagus) and payasyā (identity disputed).
notes: Elliptical: the milk cooked with these, as in unit 25, is understood but not supplied. The instrumental plural -bhiḥ stands at the end of the compound ('payasyābhiḥ'). Tāmravallī is not identified here.

words.gloss: vidārī (Pueraria tuberosa; probable); and so on; group

hindi: अथवा विदारी आदि गण से।
english: Or with the group (gaṇa) beginning with vidārī.
notes: Elliptical: milk cooked with the group is understood from unit 25 but not supplied. The members of the group are not named here.

words.gloss: śvadaṃṣṭrā (Tribulus terrestris, gokṣura); standard; svarasa (expressed fresh juice); milk; cooked

hindi: अथवा श्वदंष्ट्रा यानी गोखरू के स्वरस यानी निकाले हुए ताज़े रस और दूध में पकाया हुआ घी।
english: Or ghee (sarpis) cooked in the svarasa (expressed juice) of śvadaṃṣṭrā (caltrop) and milk.
notes: Print runs 'vā' and 'sarpiḥ' together (vāsarpiḥ). The grouping (juice of śvadaṃṣṭrā and milk, or juice and milk of ...) is not decided; the plain reading is used. Śvadaṃṣṭrā is usually gokṣura (standard); the name also covers other plants, but this is the usual one.

words.gloss: palāṇḍu (onion, Allium cepa); standard; juice; cooked

hindi: अथवा पलाण्डु यानी प्याज के रस में पकाया हुआ, शहद के साथ।
english: Or (that) cooked in the juice of palāṇḍu (onion), with honey.
notes: Elliptical: what is cooked (ghee, as in unit 28) is not stated here; no noun is supplied.

words.gloss: not; complete; three; months; of one whose three months are not complete
not; born, developed; sāra (essence, firmness); because of the state

hindi: परन्तु जिसके तीन मास पूरे नहीं हुए, उसके पुष्प यानी रक्तस्राव के दिखने पर गर्भ प्रायः नहीं टिकता, क्योंकि उसमें सार उत्पन्न नहीं हुआ होता।
english: But when puṣpa (bleeding) is seen in her whose three months are not complete, the garbha (embryo) generally does not stay, because sāra (essence, firmness) has not yet developed.
notes: 'apūrṇa-trimāsā' is a bahuvrīhi; 'months of pregnancy' is understood from garbha. 'sāra' = essence, firmness, solidity of the embryo; the exact doctrinal sense is not given. Genitive of the woman with locative absolute 'puṣpadarśane'.
lines_deva: अपूर्णत्रिमासायास्तु पुष्पदर्शने गर्भः प्रायो न तिष्ठत्यसंजातसारत्वात्
lines_iast: apūrṇatrimāsāyāstu puṣpadarśane garbhaḥ prāyo na tiṣṭhatyasaṃjātasāratvāt

words.gloss: opposed, conflicting; treatment; because of the state

hindi: और आम यानी कच्चे, अपक्व पदार्थ के अनुबन्ध में, आगे भी, विरुद्ध उपक्रम यानी परस्पर विरोधी चिकित्सा होने के कारण।
english: And in the āma-anvaye (the connection with āma, raw undigested material), even afterwards, because of conflicting (viruddha) treatment.
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue unit 30 (the embryo does not stay), with the verb carried. The sense is obscure: 'āmānvaye' read as 'in the connection / following of āma'; 'ūrdhvam api' 'even afterwards' (after three months?); 'viruddhopakramatva' read as 'because the treatments conflict' (what suits āma conflicts with what suits pregnancy). Another reading takes 'viruddha-upakrama' as 'contrary treatment'. Nothing firm is built on this.

hindi: उसमें रूक्ष और शीतल का प्रयोग करे।
english: In that case one should apply dry (rūkṣa) and cool (ones).
notes: The unstated nouns are shown as '(ones)'; unit 34 gives the list.

hindi: वह इस प्रकार है।
english: That is as follows.
notes: Introduces the list of unit 34.

words.gloss: ghana (nut-grass, Cyperus rotundus; also called mustā); probable
kaṭvaṅga (drug name, unidentified; possibly the tree śyonāka, Oroxylum indicum)
mudga (green gram, Vigna radiata); standard; and so on; soups (yūṣa)

hindi: पहले उपवास, तथा दुरालभा यानी जवासा या धमासा, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, अमृता यानी गिलोय, उशीर यानी खस, पर्पटक यानी सम्भवतः पित्तपापड़ा, घन यानी अनुमानित पाठ पर नागरमोथा, चन्दन, अतिविषा यानी अतीस, बला यानी बरियार, अनुमानित पाठ पर कट्वंग, जिसकी पहचान अज्ञात है, और धनिया के काढ़े का पान, और तृणधान्य यानी घास के अनाज, शालि तथा साठी चावल की पेया यानी पतली लपसी का भोजन, मूँग आदि के यूष के साथ; और जब आम यानी अपक्व रस जीत लिया जाए तब पहले की तरह स्निग्ध और शीतल।
english: First fasting; likewise the drinking of a decoction of durālabhā (identity disputed; Alhagi or Fagonia), amṛtā (guḍūcī, Tinospora cordifolia), uśīra (vetiver), parpaṭaka (probably Fumaria parviflora), ghana (on a conjectural reading; mustā, nut-grass), sandalwood (candana), ativiṣā (Aconitum heterophyllum), balā (Sida cordifolia), kaṭvaṅga (on a conjectural reading; unidentified) and dhānyaka (coriander); and, as food, thin gruel (peyā) of tṛṇadhānya (grass-grains), śāli and ṣaṣṭika, with soups (yūṣa) of mudga (green gram) and the like; but when āma has been overcome, unctuous and cool (ones) as before.

text_flags.why: possible: 'ghna' read as 'ghana' (a name of mustā, nut-grass); metre-free prose, sense of a fever-type decoction list fits
possible: 'kaṭuṅga' read as kaṭvaṅga (u for v); 'kātha' read as kvātha (decoction)
possible: the e after ṣaṣṭika is a print slip (ṣaṣṭika + peyām gives ṣaṣṭikapeyām)

notes: Long list: all drugs of the first compound are taken as one decoction (kvātha) taken as a drink. 'ghana' (mustā) and 'kaṭvaṅga' are conjectural readings of damaged printed forms and are marked in the English and Hindi. 'tṛṇadhānya' = grains of grasses (the text does not list which). The 'mudgādiyūṣaiḥ' soups go with the gruel/food. 'jite āme' = 'when āma has been overcome'.
lines_deva: प्रागुपवासं तथा दुरालभाऽमृतोशीरपर्पटकघ्नचंदनातिविषाबलाकटुंगधान्यककाथपानं तृणधान्यशालिषष्टिकेपेयामशनं च मुद्गादियूषैर्जिते त्वामे स्निग्धशीतानि पूर्ववत्
lines_iast: prāgupavāsaṃ tathā durālabhā'mṛtośīraparpaṭakaghnacaṃdanātiviṣābalākaṭuṃgadhānyakakāthapānaṃ tṛṇadhānyaśāliṣaṣṭikepeyāmaśanaṃ ca mudgādiyūṣairjite tvāme snigdhaśītāni pūrvavat

words.gloss: garbha (embryo); koṣṭha (storehouse, belly; probably the womb); cleansing; for the purpose of
pain, distress; forgetting; for the purpose of

hindi: परन्तु आमगर्भ यानी कच्चे गर्भ के गिर जाने पर, सामर्थ्य के अनुसार मद्य यानी नशीले पेयों में से किसी एक को पिलाए, गर्भकोष्ठ यानी गर्भ के कोष्ठ, सम्भवतः गर्भाशय, की शुद्धि के लिए और पीड़ा को भुलाने के लिए।
english: But when the āma-garbha (unripe embryo; probably an early miscarriage) has fallen, one should make (her) drink any one of the madyas (intoxicating drinks), according to capacity, for the cleansing of the garbha-koṣṭha (the 'storehouse' of the embryo, probably the womb) and for forgetting the pain (arti).
notes: Print runs 'patite' and 'madyānām' together. 'sāmarthyataḥ' = according to capacity (of the drinker, or of the physician); not decided. 'garbha-koṣṭha' = the storehouse of the embryo, probably the womb (probable). 'arti' is printed with doubled t (artti), normalised. āma-garbha appears to mean an embryo that has not yet matured, probably early pregnancy loss (probable).

words.gloss: pācanīya (digestive, promoting digestion); substance, drug; joined with
uddālaka (probably a kind of kodo millet; identity disputed); and so on; yavāgū (thick gruel)

hindi: मद्य न पीने वाले को पाचनीय द्रव्यों से युक्त, स्नेह यानी तेल या वसा और लवण से रहित, तिल सहित, उद्दालक यानी सम्भवतः कोदो की कोई किस्म, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, आदि की यवागू यानी गाढ़ी लपसियों से उपचार करे, जितने मास हों उतने दिन तक।
english: One should treat a non-drinker of madya (intoxicating drink) with yavāgūs (thick gruels) of uddālaka (identity disputed; probably a kind of kodo millet) and the like, joined with pācanīya (digestion-promoting) substances, without sneha (oil, fat) and salt, and with sesame, for as many days as there are months.
notes: Printed 'māsā stāvaṃtyahānīti' is māsās tāvanti ahāni iti with the s of the visarga attached to the following token; the first token is read as māsāḥ and the second token's words start at tāvanti. The closing 'iti' is not translated. 'As many months' is of the pregnancy (months of the fallen embryo), understood but not stated, so the translation stays literal. Uddālaka: a kind of kodo millet is a usual guess (disputed); it is also a name of Cordia in some texts.
lines_deva: अमद्यपां पाचनीयद्रव्योपहिताभिः स्नेहलोणवर्जाभिः सतिलाभिरुद्दालकादियवागूभिरुपाचरेद्यावंतो मासा स्तावंत्यहानीति

hindi: फिर तृप्त करने वाले, बल की रक्षा करने वाले, स्नेहरहित आहारों से, दोष, धातु और क्लेद की शुद्धि तक।
english: Then with foods that are gratifying (prīṇana), protective of strength and non-unctuous (without sneha), until the doṣas, dhātus and kleda are cleansed.
notes: Elliptical: the verb (upācaret) is carried from unit 36. 'ā + ablative' = 'until'. Compound 'doṣa-dhātu-kleda' may be 'the kleda of doṣa and dhātu'; the plain list reading is used. kleda = moisture, wet matter.

hindi: क्योंकि आमगर्भ के शेष रह जाने से शूल यानी पीड़ा बार-बार लगी रहेगी। इसलिए तीक्ष्ण से, और कुछ भी शेष न रखते हुए, उपचार करे।
english: For, because of a remnant of the āma-garbha, pain (śūla) would keep clinging on again and again. Therefore one should treat with sharp (tīkṣṇa) (ones), and leave no remnant.

text_flags.why: possible: ca + upācaret gives copācaret; the print has 'cupā-' (o/u matra)

notes: [02.04.38] Gives the reason for the strong measures of unit 39. 'anuṣajyeta' read as 'would persist / recur'. [02.04.39] 'tīkṣṇa' is sharp or strong; no noun is stated, so '(ones)' is used (the strong measures are not named). 'anavaśeṣayan' is a causative present participle: making nothing remain.

words.gloss: dīpanīya (kindling digestion); pācanīya (digestive); jīvanīya (life-promoting); bṛṃhaṇīya (bulk-promoting, nourishing); madhura (sweet); Vāta; removing

hindi: इसके बाद स्नेह यानी तेल या वसा के पान, बस्तियों यानी एनिमा और आहारों से, जो दीपनीय, पाचनीय, जीवनीय, बृंहणीय, मधुर और वात को हरने वाले हों।
english: After that, with drinks of sneha (oil, fat), with bastis (enemas) and with foods that are dīpanīya (digestive-fire kindling), pācanīya (digestion-promoting), jīvanīya (life-promoting), bṛṃhaṇīya (nourishing), sweet (madhura) and Vāta-removing.
notes: Elliptical: the verb (upācaret) is carried. The adjectives in the last compound are masculine plural and may qualify only the foods or all three; the translation attaches them to the foods, the nearest noun. The closing 'iti' is not translated. basti = enema in this unit.

words.gloss: of the things to be avoided

hindi: जिस स्त्री के लिए पुष्प यानी सम्भवतः रज का आना उचित हो, गर्भ के जातसार यानी सार प्राप्त कर चुकने पर, त्याज्य बातों का त्याग न करने से पुष्प का दर्शन हो, या योनि से कोई और स्राव हो।
english: In her for whom the puṣpa (the 'flower': probably menstrual-type bleeding) is due (arhati), the fetus (garbha) having acquired its essence (jātasāra), through non-avoidance of the things to be avoided there may be the sight of puṣpa, or some other flow from the yoni (vagina).
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue in the next unit (yasyāḥ here, tasyāḥ in 42); the sentence is left open. 'puṣpa' (flower) is an idiom for menstrual-type bleeding (probable, as in the earlier chunk). The sense of 'puṣpam arhati' is not firm: arhati is taken as 'is fit/due' with puṣpa as its subject; the line may also mean 'who is fit for puṣpa' (i.e. of menstruating age). jātasāra: the fetus whose sāra (essence, firmness) has arisen; not enriched. 'anyat ... yonisravaṇam' read as 'or another flow from the yoni'.
lines_deva: यस्याः पुष्पमर्हति जातसारे गर्भे वर्ज्यानामवर्जनात्पुष्पदर्शनं स्यादन्यद्वा योनिस्रवणं
lines_iast: yasyāḥ puṣpamarhati jātasāre garbhe varjyānāmavarjanātpuṣpadarśanaṃ syādanyadvā yonisravaṇaṃ

words.gram: bahuvrīhi, used as adverb, 'on that account'

words.gloss: rasa (nutrient fluid, the first dhātu); carrying
nāḍī (channel, vessel; here probably the umbilical cord, probable)

hindi: उसके लिए उसी कारण से कुपित वायु यानी वात, पित्त और श्लेष्मा यानी कफ को पकड़कर, गर्भ की रस यानी पोषक द्रव ले जाने वाली नाड़ी यानी सम्भवतः गर्भनाल को दबाकर ठहर जाता है।
english: For her, on that account, Vāyu (Vāta), provoked, having seized Pitta and Śleṣman (Kapha), presses upon the fetus's rasa-carrying nāḍī (channel, probably the umbilical cord) and stays there.
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 41 (tasyāḥ answers yasyāḥ). 'vāyu' is the wind-humour Vāta here. Reading nāḍī as the umbilical cord is probable, not stated by the word itself (nāḍī = vessel or channel). rasa = the first dhātu, nutrient fluid (doctrinal term, kept). 'garbhasya' is taken with nāḍī. pratipīḍya = pressing upon, obstructing; avatiṣṭhate = stays on.
lines_deva: तस्यास्तन्निमित्तं वायुः प्रकुपितः पित्तश्लेष्माणौ परिगृह्य गर्भस्य रसवहां नाडीं प्रतिपीड्यावतिष्ठते
lines_iast: tasyāstannimittaṃ vāyuḥ prakupitaḥ pittaśleṣmāṇau parigṛhya garbhasya rasavahāṃ nāḍīṃ pratipīḍyāvatiṣṭhate

words.gram: pres. part. a-√āp, m. nom. sg.

hindi: तब दोषों से नाड़ी यानी सम्भवतः गर्भनाल के ढक जाने पर, जैसे नहर तिनकों और पत्तों आदि से ढक जाती है, रस के ठीक से न बहने के कारण गर्भ वृद्धि को न पाता हुआ बैठ जाता है या सूख जाता है।
english: Then, the nāḍī (probably the umbilical cord) being covered over by the doṣas, as a canal (kulyā) is by grass, leaves and the like, owing to the improper carrying of rasa the fetus does not attain growth, and settles down (upaviśati) or dries up (upaśuṣyati).
notes: The locative absolute is nāḍyāṃ ... praticchannāyām. upaviśati (sits down, settles) and upaśuṣyati (dries up) anticipate the names upaviṣṭaka and upaśuṣkaka used in the following units. The simile 'as a canal by grass, leaves and the like' is in the Sanskrit (kulyāyām iva). GROUPING: appears to continue 42 (tataḥ, 'then').
lines_deva: ततो नाड्यां दोषैः कुल्यायामिव तृणपत्रादिभिः प्रतिच्छन्नायां रसस्यासम्यग्वहनाद्गर्भो वृद्धिमनाप्नुवञ्चुपविशत्युपशुष्यति वा
lines_iast: tato nāḍyāṃ doṣaiḥ kulyāyāmiva tṛṇapatrādibhiḥ praticchannāyāṃ rasasyāsamyagvahanādgarbho vṛddhimanāpnuvañcupaviśatyupaśuṣyati vā

words.gram: dvandva with adjective, m. nom. du. (corrected reading)

words.gloss: upaviṣṭaka (name of a condition; literally 'sitting down')

hindi: वहाँ जिस स्त्री में अनुमानित पाठ पर आर्तव यानी रज और परिस्राव कभी-कभी होते हैं और अल्प दिखाई देते हैं, और गर्भ माप से घटे बिना ही निरन्तर फड़कता है, तथा कुक्षि यानी पेट नहीं बढ़ता, उसे उपविष्टक कहते हैं। प्रामात् शब्द अस्पष्ट है और छोड़ा गया है।
english: Therein, in her in whom, on a conjectural reading, the ārtava (menstrual blood) and the flow (parisrāva) are occasional and are seen scanty, and the fetus constantly throbs (sphurati) without diminishing from the measure (parimāṇa), and the belly does not grow, that they call upaviṣṭaka. The word 'prāmāt' is unclear and left untranslated.

text_flags.why: possible: the printed ablative 'parisrāvāt' does not agree with the dual verb dṛśyete and dual 'alpau'; a nominative dual 'parisrāvāv alpau' (ārtava and flow, both scanty) fits, with v misread as d; compare 45, which sets 'monthly ārtava, daily flow, not very scanty' against this case
damaged or doubled: 'prāmāt' is not a known word and sits oddly before 'parimāṇāt' (perhaps a damaged pramāṇāt, 'from the standard measure'); kept unclear, not built on

notes: The printed text is doubtful in two places (see text_flags), so the translation is hedged ('on a conjectural reading') and 'prāmāt' is not translated. 'alpau' is a dual with no stated noun in the printed reading; the corrected reading makes it agree with ārtava and parisrāva. kādācitka = occasional. 'tam' is masculine: the condition or fetus is what they call upaviṣṭaka (not stated which). Orthographic normalisation recorded once here: vivarddhate -> vivardhate, arddha -> ardha (doubled consonant after r). The participle is printed aparihīyamāna with n, where the usual spelling after r is ṇ (parihīyamāṇa, as in 45); kept as printed.
lines_deva: तत्र यस्याः कादाचित्कार्त्तवपरिस्रावादल्पौ च दृश्येते सततं च गर्भः प्रामात्परिमाणादपरिहीयमानएव स्फुरति न च कुक्षिर्विवर्द्धते तमुपविष्टकमित्याचक्षते
lines_iast: tatra yasyāḥ kādācitkārttavaparisrāvādalpau ca dṛśyete satataṃ ca garbhaḥ prāmātparimāṇādaparihīyamānaeva sphurati na ca kukṣirvivarddhate tamupaviṣṭakamityācakṣate

hindi: जब प्रत्येक मास आर्तव या प्रतिदिन परिस्रवण बहुत थोड़ा न हो, और इस प्रकार क्षीण होता हुआ गर्भ देर से कुछ हिलता है।
english: When, however, there is ārtava (menstrual blood) every month or flow (parisravaṇa) every day, not very scanty, and so the fetus, wasting (parihīyamāṇa), moves a little after a long time.

text_flags.why: possible: 'garbhāś' (plural nominative) does not agree with the singular verb spandate; garbhaś is expected, so the long ā looks like a print slip

notes: Elliptical: the first clause has no verb (a copula 'is' is understood and not supplied). 'ca tathā' read as 'and so, and likewise'. This appears to be the second (milder) picture beside 44. parihīyamāṇa is the passive participle of pari-√hā, 'being diminished, wasting'. The text does not say here what condition is named; the names appear in 46. GROUPING: the 'yadā' clause appears to be completed in 46 ('tad upaśuṣkakaṃ nāgodaraṃ ca'); the sentence runs across the two units.
lines_deva: यदा तु प्रतिमासमार्तवं प्रत्यहं वा परिस्रवणं नात्यल्पं चतथा परिहीयमाणो गर्भाश्चिरात्किंचित्स्पंदते
lines_iast: yadā tu pratimāsamārtavaṃ pratyahaṃ vā parisravaṇaṃ nātyalpaṃ catathā parihīyamāṇo garbhāścirātkiṃcitspaṃdate

hindi: और कुक्षि यानी पेट बढ़ा हुआ होकर भी घटता है, वह उपशुष्कक है और नागोदर भी।
english: And the belly (kukṣi), though grown, diminishes: that is upaśuṣkaka, and nāgodara.

text_flags.why: near certain: c for p; the verb is pari-√hā (as in 44 and 45)

notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 44-45. Copula 'is' understood and not supplied. nāgodara is kept as a name (literally 'nāga-belly'; nāga can be serpent or elephant); the text does not explain it and it is not enriched. Whether 'upaśuṣkaka' and 'nāgodara' are two names for one condition or two conditions is not settled by the wording.
lines_deva: कुक्षिश्च वृद्धोऽपि चरिहीयते तदुपशुष्ककं नागोदरं च
lines_iast: kukṣiśca vṛddho'pi carihīyate tadupaśuṣkakaṃ nāgodaraṃ ca

hindi: वे दोनों माता के आहार के अल्प तेज से पोषण पाते हुए जब पुष्ट हो जाएँ, तब वर्षों के समूहों के बाद भी स्त्री प्रसव करती ही है।
english: Those two, however, nourished by the slight tejas (vigour) of the mother's food, when they become well-nourished, then even after groups of years the woman (pramadā) gives birth indeed.
notes: 'tau' (dual) is read as the two kinds of fetus just described (upaviṣṭaka and upaśuṣkaka); the line does not name them. 'tejas' of food is kept as 'vigour'; it could also be read as 'essence'. varṣagaṇa = groups of years (a long time); no number is stated. 'prasūyate' is taken as the middle present, 'bears, gives birth'.
lines_deva: तौ तु मातुराहारतेजसाऽल्पेनाप्यायमानौ यदा पुष्टौ स्यातां तदा वर्षगणैरपि प्रमदा प्रसूयत एव

words.gloss: cracked; discoloured; rough; skin; the state of

hindi: वहाँ वात से उपविष्टक और उपशुष्कक में वायु का प्रतिघात होता है यानी वह रुकता है; मल शब्द सहित, झागदार और टूटा हुआ निकलता है; मूत्र रुकता है; कमर, पीठ और हृदय में पीड़ा और जम्हाई होती है; नींद का नाश, बार-बार प्रतिश्याय यानी जुकाम, सूखी खाँसी और थकावट होती है; मानो दोनों कान भनभनाते हैं, मानो दोनों कनपटियाँ चुभती हैं; शरीर मानो चींटियों से जुड़ा हुआ है; मानो काटता हुआ वायु कुक्षि यानी पेट में घूमता है; मानो अन्धकार में प्रवेश कराया जाता है; अन्न का पाचन कठिनाई से होता है; दिन-प्रतिदिन हानि होती है; और त्वचा का फटा हुआ, विवर्ण और रूखा होना होता है।
english: Therein, in upaviṣṭaka and upaśuṣkaka, by Vāta, the vāyu is obstructed; dung (śakṛt) is passed noisy, frothy and broken; urine is held back; there are pain in the waist, back and heart (hṛdaya), and yawning; loss of sleep, repeated pratiśyāya (nasal catarrh), dry cough and lassitude (sāda); the two ears, as it were, hum, the two temples are, as it were, pricked; the body is, as it were, joined with ants; as if cutting about, vāyu wanders in the belly (kukṣi); one is, as it were, made to enter darkness (tamas); digestion of food is with difficulty; there is decline day after day; and there is the state of cracked, discoloured, rough skin.
notes: The construction 'vātena upaviṣṭakopaśuṣkakayoḥ' is loose (in these two, by Vāta); kept literal. 'abhīkṣṇam' may qualify nidrānāśa or pratiśyāya; placed with pratiśyāya. 'tamaḥ praveśa' (entering darkness) is a known symptom phrase (giddiness, blackout), probable. 'pipīlikābhir iva saṃsṛjyate' describes a crawling sensation, probable; kept literal. 'hṛdaya' = heart (standard); 'kaṭī' = waist or loins. pratiśyāya = nasal catarrh (standard). sāda = lassitude. The last compound ends in 'tvakttvaṃ' (doubled t is orthographic, tvak-tvam, recorded once here). The subject of 'bhavati' is the list of states; the woman is not named in this unit. Reading note: the printed Devanagari is तमइव (tama iva, regular sandhi with hiatus), so the word is iva 'as it were' (a simile like the others in the unit), not 'tamaiva'/'tamaḥ eva'; no text flag is needed. Whether 'tamaḥ praveśyate' means 'one is made to enter darkness' or 'darkness is brought on' is not settled by the wording.
lines_deva: तत्र वातेनोपविष्टकोपशुष्ककयोर्वायुः प्रतिहन्यते सशब्दं फेनिलं विच्छिन्नं शकृदुपवेश्यते मूत्रमुपरुध्यते कटीपृष्ठहृदयेषु वेदनाजृंभा निद्रानाशोऽभीक्ष्णं प्रतिश्यायः शुष्ककासः सादः क्ष्वेलेते इवकर्णौ तुद्येते इव शंखौ पिपीलिकाभिरिव संसृज्यते शरीरं परिकृंतन्निव वायुर्भ्रमति कुक्षौ तमइव प्रवेश्यते दुःखेनान्नस्य जरणमहरहः परिहानिः स्फुटितविवर्णपरुषत्वक्त्त्वं च भवति
lines_iast: tatra vātenopaviṣṭakopaśuṣkakayorvāyuḥ pratihanyate saśabdaṃ phenilaṃ vicchinnaṃ śakṛdupaveśyate mūtramuparudhyate kaṭīpṛṣṭhahṛdayeṣu vedanājṛṃbhā nidrānāśo'bhīkṣṇaṃ pratiśyāyaḥ śuṣkakāsaḥ sādaḥ kṣvelete ivakarṇau tudyete iva śaṃkhau pipīlikābhiriva saṃsṛjyate śarīraṃ parikṛṃtanniva vāyurbhramati kukṣau tamaiva praveśyate duḥkhenānnasya jaraṇamaharahaḥ parihāniḥ sphuṭitavivarṇaparuṣatvakttvaṃ ca bhavati

hindi: पित्त से ताम्र-हरित निकलता है; धूमिक और अम्लक, जिनका अर्थ अनिश्चित है; वमन, मूर्च्छा, कुक्षि और हृदय में जलन; आँखों, मूत्र और नखों का पीले, लाल और गोमूत्र की आभा वाले होना; और स्त्री काली, दुर्बल और नित्य पीड़ा वाली हो जाती है।
english: By Pitta, a coppery-green (one) is passed; dhūmika and amlaka (words of uncertain sense, 'smoky' and 'sour'); vomiting (chardi); fainting (mūrcchā); burning in the belly and heart (hṛdaya); the state of the eyes, urine and nails being yellow, red and cow-urine-hued; and the woman becomes dark (kālī), weak and constantly in pain (śūla).
notes: Elliptical: the noun of 'tāmraharitam' is not stated; śakṛt (dung) of 48 is the likely understood noun and is not supplied. 'dhūmika' and 'amlaka' are kept untranslated in sense: they may be a smoky and a sour sensation or taste, but this is not firm. 'pīta-rakta-gomūtrābha' may also be read as 'yellow-red, or cow-urine-hued'; the plainer list is kept. 'tva' is the abstract on the whole list of netra, mūtra, nakha. mūrcchā = fainting (standard).
lines_deva: पित्तेन ताम्रहरितमुपवेश्यते धूमिकोऽम्लकश्छर्दिर्मूर्च्छा कुक्षिहृदयदाहः पीतरक्तगोमूत्राभनेत्रमूत्रनखत्वं काली दुर्बला नित्यशूला च नारी भवति
lines_iast: pittena tāmraharitamupaveśyate dhūmiko'mlakaśchardirmūrcchā kukṣihṛdayadāhaḥ pītaraktagomūtrābhanetramūtranakhatvaṃ kālī durbalā nityaśūlā ca nārī bhavati

words.gloss: white; hand; foot; eye; the state

hindi: श्लेष्मा यानी कफ से: मुख की मधुरता, उत्क्लेश यानी मिचली, कफ का उगलना, भोजन से द्वेष, हाथ, पैर और आँखों का श्वेत होना, खाँसी और श्वास यानी साँस फूलना।
english: By Śleṣman (Kapha): the state of a sweet mouth, nausea (utkleśa), vomiting up of phlegm, aversion to food, whiteness of the hands, feet and eyes, cough, and breathlessness (śvāsa).
notes: Elliptical: no verb, as in 49 (the list continues the Vāta and Pitta pictures of 48-49). utkleśa = nausea (standard). 'śleṣmodvamana' = bringing up phlegm; the print gives no word for 'vomiting' other than udvamana. śvāsa = laboured breathing (asthma-type, probable), kept as breathlessness.
lines_deva: श्लेष्मणा मधुरास्यत्वमुत्क्लेशः श्लेष्मोद्वमनं भक्तद्वेषः श्वेतहस्तपादनेत्रता कासः श्वासश्च
lines_iast: śleṣmaṇā madhurāsyatvamutkleśaḥ śleṣmodvamanaṃ bhaktadveṣaḥ śvetahastapādanetratā kāsaḥ śvāsaśca

words.gloss: of those two, for those two

hindi: उन दोनों के लिए जीवनीय यानी जीवन देने वाले, बृंहणीय यानी पुष्ट करने वाले और मधुर औषधों से पकाए हुए घृतों का उपयोग।
english: For those two, the use of ghees (sarpis) cooked with life-promoting (jīvanīya), nourishing (bṛṃhaṇīya) and sweet (madhura) medicines (auṣadha).
notes: GROUPING: appears to begin the treatment of 44-50. Elliptical: no verb (the use 'is to be made' is understood and not supplied). 'tayoḥ' is taken as the two conditions (upaviṣṭaka and upaśuṣkaka). jīvanīya and bṛṃhaṇīya are classes of drugs; the members are not listed here. 'sarpiṣām' is a plural: more than one ghee.

words.gloss: of rasas (juices or broths; sense open)
raw, unripe; fetus, embryo (āmagarbha; exact sense uncertain)

hindi: वैसे ही दूधों, रसों और आमगर्भों का गर्भ की वृद्धि करने वाला।
english: Likewise, (the use) of milks (payas), rasas (juices or broths) and āmagarbhas (literally 'raw fetuses'; exact sense uncertain) is promoting the growth of the fetus.

text_flags.why: near certain: 'viddhi' (piercing) makes no sense here; vṛddhi (growth) is needed after 'garbha', in line with 47 and 59-60, and ṛ misread as i is a plausible print slip

notes: Elliptical: the masculine 'karaḥ' agrees with 'upayogaḥ' of 51, which is understood and shown in parentheses in English only. 'rasa' here may mean meat-broth or other juices; not settled. 'āmagarbha' (raw/unripe fetus or embryo) is kept as printed; the text does not say whose, and the sense is not enriched. It recurs in 63.

hindi: वैसे ही इन्हीं घृत आदि के साथ भोजन कराना।
english: Likewise, feeding (saṃbhojana) with these very (ones), with ghee and the others.
notes: Elliptical: no verb. 'etaiḥ ... ghṛtādibhiḥ': the nouns are not stated; 'these very ones' is read as ghee and the like. The recipient of the feeding is not stated (the woman is the natural reading).

words.gloss: carriage, riding; vehicle, conveyance; and others
shaking, jolting; rubbing, wiping; yawning, stretching

hindi: भली-भाँति भोजन पाने वाली का बार-बार यान, वाहन आदि से, तथा क्षोभण यानी हिलाने, मार्जन यानी रगड़ने और जृम्भण यानी जम्हाई से उपपादन।
english: Of one well provided with food (subhikṣā), repeatedly, the bringing about (upapādana) by means of carriages, vehicles and the like, and by shaking (kṣobhaṇa), rubbing (mārjana) and yawning (jṛmbhaṇa).
notes: The sense is not firm. 'subhikṣāyāḥ' (of a woman with plentiful food) is taken with the woman understood; the object of 'upapādanam' is not stated; and whether the instrumentals 'kṣobhaṇa-mārjana-jṛmbhaṇaiḥ' are means of the bringing about (parallel to 'yānavāhanādibhiḥ') or what is brought about is open. Elliptical: no verb. mārjana can mean wiping or rubbing; jṛmbhaṇa yawning or stretching.

hindi: फिर विशेष रूप से वात में पहले ही सैन्धव यानी सेंधा नमक से युक्त दूध की बस्ति यानी एनिमा देकर, ठंडे जल से नहाई हुई को मृदु शालि का भात खिलाए।
english: Then, especially in Vāta, first of all, having given a milk-basti (enema) provided with saindhava (rock salt), one should feed her, bathed in cold water, soft boiled śāli rice (śāli-odana).

text_flags.why: near certain: 'strāta' is not a word; snāta (bathed) is needed, st for sn is a plausible print slip (the same in 80)
possible: the absolutive of √dā is dattvā; 'datvā' with one t looks like a print habit or slip

notes: basti = enema here (a milk enema, given with the salt). 'her' is the accusative feminine 'snātām' (the woman is understood). 'mṛdu' is taken with the rice (soft). 'viśeṣeṇa vāte' = especially in the Vāta case. śāli = a winter rice (standard); odana = boiled rice.
lines_deva: अथ विशेषेण वाते पूर्वमेव सैंधवोपहितं क्षीरबस्तिं दत्वा शीतोदकस्त्रातां मृदु शाल्योदनं भोजयेत्
lines_iast: atha viśeṣeṇa vāte pūrvameva saiṃdhavopahitaṃ kṣīrabastiṃ datvā śītodakastrātāṃ mṛdu śālyodanaṃ bhojayet

words.gloss: vidārī (Pueraria tuberosa, probable); and the others; group (gaṇa); prepared

hindi: फिर विदारी यानी सम्भवतः विदारीकन्द आदि के समूह से तैयार किए घी से अनुवासन यानी चिकनाई वाली बस्ति दे।
english: Then one should give an anuvāsana (unctuous enema) with ghee (sarpis) prepared with the vidārī-and-others group (vidārī-ādi-gaṇa; vidārī probably Indian kudzu, Pueraria tuberosa).
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 55 (Vāta case). vidārī: Pueraria tuberosa (probable); the members of the vidārī-ādi group are not listed here. anuvāsayet: an anuvāsana is an oil or ghee enema (standard), kept as 'give an anuvāsana'. sādhita = prepared (glossary).

hindi: और निवात यानी वायु से बचाव का सेवन करे।
english: And one should resort to shelter from the wind (nivāta).
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 55-56. nivāta (n.) = wind-sheltered state or place; not enriched.

words.gloss: madhuka (licorice, Glycyrrhiza glabra, probable); vidārī (see 56); decoction (niryūha); cooked

hindi: पित्त में मधुक यानी सम्भवतः मुलेठी और विदारी यानी सम्भवतः विदारीकन्द के निर्यूह यानी काढ़े से पकाया हुआ दूध पिए।
english: In Pitta, one should drink milk cooked with a decoction (niryūha) of madhuka (probably licorice) and vidārī (probably Indian kudzu).
notes: madhuka = licorice (Glycyrrhiza glabra), probable; the word can also mean the mahua tree (Madhuca longifolia), so it is hedged. niryūha = decoction; siddha = cooked. 'cooked with a decoction' is read as milk prepared with the decoction.

words.gloss: husked, without husk; māṣa (black gram, Vigna mungo, standard); āḍhaka (a measure)

hindi: उसके सिद्ध न होने पर वीरण यानी सम्भवतः खस की घास, शालि यानी धान, कुश यानी कुशा घास, काश यानी काँस, इक्षुवालिका, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, वेतस, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, और परिव्याध, जिसकी पहचान अज्ञात है, इनकी जड़ों का, तथा भूतिका, जिसकी पहचान अज्ञात है, अनुमानित पाठ पर अनन्त यानी सम्भवतः सारिवा, काश्मर्य यानी गम्भारी, परूषक यानी फालसा, मधुक यानी सम्भवतः मुलेठी और मृद्वीका यानी अंगूर का, दूध और आधे जल के साथ रस निकालकर, उससे, पियाल यानी सम्भवतः चिरौंजी और बिभीतक यानी बहेड़े की गिरी तथा तिल की लुगदी से युक्त, थोड़े नमकीन और गरम रस से निरूह दे।
english: If that does not succeed, having extracted, with milk and half water, the rasa (decoction) of the roots of vīraṇa (probably vetiver grass), śāli (rice), kuśa (kusha grass), kāśa (kans grass), ikṣuvālikā (identity disputed), vetasa (identity disputed) and parivyādha (unidentified), and of bhūtikā (unidentified), ananta (on a conjectural reading; probably sārivā), kāśmarya (gmelina), parūṣaka (phalsa), madhuka (probably licorice) and mṛdvīkā (grape), one should give a nirūha (decoction enema) with that, combined with a paste (kalka) of the kernels (majjā) of piyāla (probably Buchanania) and bibhītaka and of sesame (tila), slightly salty and warm.

notes: A long list, read as two groups. 'mūlānām' is taken with the first group (roots); the second group stands in the genitive without 'mūla' and may be whole drugs or roots, not settled. 'ikṣubālikā' is read as one name (ikṣuvālikā, v/b interchange). Identifications: vīraṇa probable (the grass whose root is uśīra), kuśa, kāśa, śāli, kāśmarya, parūṣaka, mṛdvīkā, bibhītaka standard; ananta probable but hedged because the reading is conjectural; piyāla probable (Buchanania lanzan); ikṣuvālikā and vetasa disputed; parivyādha and bhūtikā unidentified. majjā = kernel (glossary). 'tad-asiddhau' = if that (the anuvāsana) does not succeed, taken from the context. nirūha = decoction enema (standard); the rasa is the extract. The grammar 'tena ... yuktena ... nirūhayet' puts the paste in the extract.

hindi: और जिसका विबन्ध यानी कब्ज दूर हो गया हो, जो नहा चुकी और खा चुकी हो, उसे सायंकाल उसी तेल से अनुवासन दे। उदावर्त यानी वात का उलटा ऊपर की ओर चलना, यदि उपेक्षित हो, तो अचानक गर्भ सहित गर्भवती स्त्री को नष्ट कर दे।
english: And, her whose constipation (vibandha) has gone, who has bathed and eaten, one should give in the evening an anuvāsana (unctuous enema) with that very oil. Udāvarta (a disorder in which Vāta runs upward in reverse), if neglected, would suddenly destroy the pregnant woman together with her fetus.

text_flags.why: near certain: 'strāta' is not a word; snāta (bathed) fits, as in 55

notes: [02.04.80] GROUPING: appears to continue 78-79. 'tena eva tailena' = the oil of 78 (madhuraka-cooked oil); that identification follows from the context and is not stated. aśita = having eaten. [02.04.81] Printed udāvartto (rtt) is the book-wide orthographic normalisation. atipātayet = literally 'would cause to fall away'; 'destroy' is the plain sense; 'cause to miscarry' is a possible narrower reading, since the object is the woman together with her fetus. Hindi uses वात for the doṣa. Modern equivalent (probable): udāvarta = reversal of the downward course of Vāta with retention of stool and wind, roughly an obstructive bowel disorder (constipation or ileus type).

hindi: जिस स्त्री का गर्भ, फिर दोषों के अत्यधिक संचय से, या कहे हुए व्यवाय यानी मैथुन आदि से, या अन्य रोगों से, या माता और सन्तान के पहले संचित कर्म से, बन्धन से छूट जाता है, जैसे फल डंठल से; वह बन्धन से छूटा हुआ गर्भ गर्भशय्या यानी सम्भवतः गर्भाशय को लाँघकर यकृत्, प्लीहा यानी तिल्ली और आँतों के छिद्रों में लटकता हुआ कोष्ठ में क्षोभ उत्पन्न करता है।
english: Of her whose fetus (garbha) is released from its bond, whether by an excessive accumulation of doṣas, or by those stated, vyavāya (sexual intercourse) and the like, or by other diseases, or by the earlier accumulated action of the mother and of the offspring, like a fruit from its stalk: that fetus, with its bond released, having passed beyond the bed of the fetus (garbhaśayyā, probably the womb), hanging in the gaps of the liver (yakṛt), spleen (plīha) and intestines (antra), brings about a disturbance of the koṣṭha (storehouse, belly).

text_flags.why: possible: the passive of √muc is mucyate; printed 'mocyate' (with o) may be a print slip, though a guṇa form could be an old variant

notes: One long sentence; the main clause begins at 'saḥ'. 'yathoktair vā vyavāyādibhir' is taken as 'or by those stated, vyavāya and the like'; the grammar could also join 'yathokta' with 'vyādhibhiḥ', so the scope of 'stated' is not firm. 'pūrvopacitena karmaṇā' = by earlier accumulated action (karman); the doctrinal sense is not expanded. garbhaśayyā = bed of the fetus, probably the womb (probable). The instrumental 'vivaraiḥ' with avalambamānaḥ is rendered loosely as 'in the gaps'. koṣṭha = storehouse, belly. The sentence is followed by 83, which continues the account. Genitive 'yasyāḥ' stands loosely with 'garbhaḥ' ('of whom the fetus'). Printed 'baṃdhanānmocyate' reads mocyate (guṇa vowel).

hindi: तब कोष्ठ के क्षोभ से अपान वायु बार-बार कुक्षि, बस्ति यानी सम्भवतः मूत्राशय, पार्श्व, उदर और योनि में पीड़ा, आनाह यानी पेट फूलना, तथा मल और मूत्र का रुकना उत्पन्न करके कोमल गर्भ को रक्त के रूप में गिरा देती है।
english: Then, from the disturbance of the koṣṭha, the Apāna wind (vāyu), having repeatedly brought about pain in the flank (kukṣi), basti (probably the bladder), sides, belly and yoni, distension (ānāha), and retentions of stool and urine, causes the young fetus to fall away in the form of blood.
notes: Compound 'kukṣi...yoni-śūla-ānāha-viṇ-mūtra-saṅgān' is read as: pain in kukṣi, basti, sides, belly and yoni; ānāha; retention of stool and of urine (the scope of 'śūla' over the five places is a reading, not certain). basti = bladder is probable (basti also names the enema device). ānāha = distension of the belly with retention of stool and wind (standard). 'śoṇitabhāvena' = literally 'by the state of blood', taken as 'in the form of blood'. Continues 82 (GROUPING: appears to continue 82).

english: That has been stated before.
notes: The referent of 'saḥ' (masculine) is not named in the unit; the text does not say what has been stated before (possibly the abortion, garbhasrāva, or the wind); not enriched. The printed so'bhihitaḥ = saḥ abhihitaḥ (regular sandhi). GROUPING: appears to continue 83.

hindi: पर गर्भ के बढ़ जाने पर पेट कठोर, स्थिर, ठण्डा और मानो भीतर पत्थर वाला दिखाई देता है।
english: But when the fetus (garbha) has grown, the belly (udara) appears stiff, still, cold, as if it had a stone inside.
notes: Printed 'garbhestabdhaṃ' joins garbhe and stabdham (spacing slip, no flag). The locative absolute 'vivṛddhe garbhe' is read as 'the fetus having grown'. stimita = still, motionless (it can also mean 'wet', not chosen). aśmagarbha = literally 'stone-interior'. The unit describes the belly in the case taken up in 86 (the dead fetus); the text does not say so here.

hindi: अत्यधिक पीड़ा होती है और गर्भ हिलता नहीं, अन्य प्रकट होते हैं, योनि से स्राव नहीं होता, और अनुमानित पाठ पर इसकी दोनों आँखें धँस जाती हैं; वैसे ही वह अरति यानी बेचैनी से अत्यन्त घिरी हुई कष्ट पाती है, अन्य प्रकार से चेष्टा करती है, निढाल होती है, थकती है, दिन-रात रोती है, सोती नहीं, प्रत्येक श्वास पर कठिनाई से साँस लेती है, अत्यन्त कष्ट से जीती है और क्षीण होती है; ऐसी स्त्री को मृतगर्भा यानी मरे गर्भ वाली जाने।
english: Pain arises in excess, and the fetus does not move; other (ones) appear; the yoni does not flow; and, on a conjectural reading, her two eyes sink in; likewise she, greatly beset by arati (restlessness), is distressed, acts differently, languishes, tires, weeps day and night, does not sleep, breathes with difficulty at each breath, lives (breathes) in great distress, and wastes away. One should know a woman of this kind to be mṛtagarbhā (one with a dead fetus).

text_flags.why: possible: 'saṃsyete' is not a known verb form; saṃsīdete (they sink in) or sraṃsete (they droop) would suit the dual subject akṣiṇī; the word is doubtful
possible: svapiti is the usual 3 sg. of √svap; 'svapniti' looks like a print slip (n inserted)

notes: The verb 'saṃsyete' is not a known form: a dual verb is needed for the dual subject 'akṣiṇī' (two eyes); saṃ-sad (saṃsīdete, 'sink in') is a conjecture only, so the translation says 'on a conjectural reading'. 'anyāni' = other (signs), the noun is not stated and is shown as '(ones)'. 'yoniḥ' is taken as the subject of 'na sravati' (no flow from the yoni). 'pratyucchvāsāt kṛcchrāt' is rendered 'at each breath, with difficulty' (ablatives used loosely). 'svapniti' is printed; the standard form is svapiti. 'kṣayati' = wastes away is probable (√kṣi, dwindle); 'prāṇiti' = breathes/lives. tāmyati/śrāmyati: languishes/tires (exact shade of tāmyati is not firm). 'arati' = restlessness, discontent. The closing 'iti' follows 'kṣayati' (end of the list of signs). Dead-fetus signs as printed are translated without comment on modern medicine. Other conjectural repairs for saṃsyete (all unproven): saṃśīyete (they shrink; s/ś confusion) or saṃsyandete (they flow). The verb stays unclear. Modern equivalent (probable): mṛtagarbhā = woman carrying a dead fetus (intrauterine fetal death).

hindi: उस गर्भ को, जो कभी-कभी गलत ढंग से अनेक प्रकार से सन्तान के मार्ग यानी सम्भवतः प्रसव-मार्ग में पहुँचा हो, बिगड़ी हुई वायु से पीड़ित और मोहित हो, मूढगर्भ कहते हैं।
english: That fetus (garbha), however, which sometimes has entered the path of the offspring (apatyapatha, probably the birth passage) wrongly and in many ways, afflicted and bewildered by deranged wind (vāyu), they call mūḍhagarbha.
notes: mūḍha = bewildered, stuck; the compound is left as the technical name mūḍhagarbha. 'apatyapatha' = path of the offspring, probably the birth passage (probable). The printed run-together 'garbhaṃkadācidasamyagapatyapathamanekadhā' is read as garbham kadācit asamyak apatya-patham anekadhā. The printed 'pīḍitaṃmohitaṃ' joins two words (spacing). Modern equivalent (probable): mūḍhagarbha = obstructed labour with a malpositioned or stuck fetus (malpresentation); kept as the technical term in the translation.

notes: Elliptical: the verb 'they call' is carried from 87 and not supplied; the unstated noun is shown as '(one)'. GROUPING: appears to continue 87. notes: The printed 'tānyatraivottaratra' = tāni atra eva uttaratra (regular sandhi). The unit does not say what 'those' are; unit 90 (the eight positions) comes just before, and no pairing is asserted.

words.gloss: saṃvaraṇa (closing, covering; the thing closed is not stated)

hindi: उन सब में भी, जिसकी इन्द्रियों के विषय उलटे हो गए हों और जो आक्षेप यानी ऐंठन, योनि के खिसकने, संवरण और मक्कल, जिनका अर्थ यहाँ अस्पष्ट है, श्वास यानी साँस की तकलीफ और भ्रम यानी चक्कर से ग्रस्त हो, तथा जिसका शरीर ठण्डा और जिसकी डकारें दुर्गन्धित हों, उस स्त्री को छोड़ दे।
english: In all of those too, one should avoid the woman whose sense-objects are reversed, who is overtaken by ākṣepa (convulsion), slipping of the yoni, saṃvaraṇa (sense unclear), makkala (sense unclear), breathing trouble and giddiness, whose body is cold, and who has foul belching.
notes: The long compound 'viparītendriyārthām…abhipannām' is taken as one adjective chain for the woman: 'whose sense-objects are reversed' and 'overtaken by' the listed items. saṃvaraṇa and makkala are kept untranslated: saṃvaraṇa means closing or covering (what closes is not said) and makkala is a rare word (in other texts it names a post-delivery pain or clotted blood); neither sense is sure here. 'śvāsa' is rendered 'breathing trouble' as part of a list of troubles; it may also be plain 'breathing'. 'varjayet' = avoid; the unit does not say what is to be avoided in dealing with her (for example the operations of the following units); no object is supplied. The woman's identity (the mūḍhagarbha case) is understood from context.
lines_deva: तेषु सर्वेष्वपि विपरीतेंद्रियार्थामाक्षेपयोनिस्रंशसंवरणमक्कलश्वासभ्रमाभिपन्नां शीतगात्रां पूत्युद्गारां च वर्जयेत्
lines_iast: teṣu sarveṣvapi viparīteṃdriyārthāmākṣepayonisraṃśasaṃvaraṇamakkalaśvāsabhramābhipannāṃ śītagātrāṃ pūtyudgārāṃ ca varjayet

words.gram: m. acc. sg. used as ind.

hindi: पर गर्भशल्य यानी गर्भ के काँटे की क्षण भर भी उपेक्षा न करे। क्योंकि वह शीघ्र ही माता को दम घोंटकर मार देगा।
english: But one should not neglect the garbhaśalya (the fetus as a dart) even for a moment. For that, having made (her) breathless, would quickly kill the mother.
notes: [02.04.93] garbhaśalya is kept as the technical word: śalya = dart, thorn, or foreign body lodged in the body; 'garbha-śalya' is read as the fetus acting as a śalya. The English 'as a dart' only explains the compound. [02.04.94] The printed 'taddhinirucchvāsīkṛtyāśu' = tat hi nirucchvāsī-kṛtya āśu. 'tat' (neuter) is taken to refer to the garbhaśalya of 93; 'āśu' may belong either to the making breathless or to the killing (it is placed between). The 'her' of 'made her breathless' is not in the Sanskrit and is shown in brackets; the mother is the natural object. Hindi 'दम घोंटकर' renders nirucchvāsī-kṛtya (making breathless).

words.gram: pres. pass. part. vi-√dṝ, m. nom. sg.

hindi: और चेतना वाला गर्भ शस्त्र से चीरा जाता हुआ अंगों को विषम रूप से इधर-उधर फेंके।
english: And a fetus (garbha) that has consciousness, while being split open with a śastra (cutting instrument), may throw its limbs about unevenly.
notes: sacetana = having consciousness, alive; the unit does not say how this is known. 'viṣamam' is taken as an adverb (unevenly, irregularly); it could also be the neuter object 'uneven limbs'. The printed 'sacetanaśca' = sacetanaḥ ca.
lines_deva: सचेतनश्च गर्भः शस्त्रेण विदार्यमाणो विषममंगानि विक्षिपेत्
lines_iast: sacetanaśca garbhaḥ śastreṇa vidāryamāṇo viṣamamaṃgāni vikṣipet

words.gloss: unclear (printed form; on a conjectural reading 'for delivery')

hindi: इसलिए उसके अटकने पर अनुमानित पाठ पर प्रसव के लिए प्रयत्न करें, और पहले कहे हुए मन्त्र और औषध प्रयोग में लाए।
english: Therefore, in the obstruction (saṅga) of that, on a conjectural reading, they should strive for delivery, and one should apply the earlier-stated mantras and medicines (auṣadha).

text_flags.why: possible: 'sūtyaḥ' (visarga) does not fit; the dative sūtyai ('for delivery') suits 'prayateran'

notes: The printed 'sūtyaḥ' does not fit the grammar (a plural nominative 'sūtayaḥ' is not needed); 'sūtyai' (dative, 'for delivery') is conjectured, with the subject of 'prayateran' (they) not stated. 'tatsaṅge' = in the obstruction of that; the referent of 'that' (the fetus or its sticking) is not stated, and saṅga is taken up in 97. The shift from plural 'prayateran' to singular 'prayuñjīta' is noted. 'pūrvoktāni' is taken with both mantras and medicines; the earlier passage it points to is not named here.
lines_deva: तस्मात्तत्संगे सूत्यः प्रयतेरन् पूर्वोक्तानि च मंत्रौषधानि प्रयुंजीत
lines_iast: tasmāttatsaṃge sūtyaḥ prayateran pūrvoktāni ca maṃtrauṣadhāni prayuṃjīta

hindi: सङ्ग तीन प्रकार का होता है।
english: The obstruction (saṅga), however, is of three kinds.
notes: Printed 'trividhastu' = trividhaḥ tu. saṅga = sticking, obstruction (of the fetus, understood from 96).

hindi: सिर में, कन्धे में, या जघन यानी कूल्हे के भाग में।
english: In the head, in the shoulder, or in the jaghana (hip region).
notes: Elliptical: no verb; GROUPING: appears to continue 97 (the three kinds of saṅga). jaghana = hip region (loins, buttocks); the exact part is not defined here. Printed 'śirasyaṃse' = śirasi aṃse (regular sandhi). Whether the three are 'the three kinds' is not stated. Obstetric reading (probable, not stated by the text): the three kinds of saṅga correspond to head, shoulder and breech (buttock) obstruction; 'jaghana' here = hip/buttock region.

words.gloss: afterbirth (jarāyu); causing to fall; commonness, same

hindi: मूढगर्भ में तो जरायु यानी जेर को गिराने के समान कर्म है, ऐसा कुछ लोग कहते हैं। मन्त्र आदि का कर्म अथर्ववेद में बताया गया है, ऐसा कुछ लोग कहते हैं।
english: For a mūḍhagarbha, however, the procedure (karma) is the same as the causing of the jarāyu (afterbirth) to fall, some say. Some say that the procedure beginning with mantras is prescribed in the Atharvaveda.

text_flags.why: near certain: 'karmārtharva' has an extra r; karma + atharva = karmātharva (the Atharvaveda)

notes: [02.04.99] Elliptical: the verb 'say' (āhuḥ) is not stated; 'some say' is the sense of 'iti eke'. jarāyu = afterbirth, placenta/membranes (standard); the earlier glossary uses aparā for placenta. 'sāmānya' is rendered 'the same as', its plain sense is 'common to'. This is one opinion of three given in 99-101; the text does not say which is held. [02.04.100] Printed 'karmārtharvaveda…' has an extra r (karma + atharva gives karmātharva), see flag. 'Atharvaveda-vihita' is taken as 'prescribed in/by the Atharvaveda'. 'ādi' = beginning with; the other steps are not listed. The printed 'maṃtrādikarmārtharvavedavihitam' is one token.

hindi: देखे हुए कर्म वाले, शल्य निकालने वाले के द्वारा शल्य यानी काँटे या भीतर फँसी वस्तु का निकालना है, ऐसा कुछ लोग कहते हैं। वास्तव में शस्त्रकर्म यानी शस्त्र से किया जाने वाला कर्म सबसे कठिन है।
english: Some say: the extraction of the śalya (dart, foreign body) is by a śalya-remover (śalyahartṛ) whose work has been seen (dṛṣṭakarman). In truth, śastrakarma (work with the cutting instrument, surgery) is the most difficult.
notes: [02.04.101] Copula understood. 'dṛṣṭakarman' = one whose work has been seen (an experienced practitioner); not enriched. 'śalyahartṛ' = remover of the śalya (a surgeon, probable); the fetus is the śalya in this context (see 93), not stated here. 'iti eke' = some (say). [02.04.102] kaṣṭatama is rendered 'most difficult' (kaṣṭa = hard, painful, troublesome); 'most painful' is also possible. The modern word 'surgery' stands beside the Sanskrit term only to name it.

words.gloss: yoni; liver (yakṛt); spleen (plīha); intestines (antra); womb (garbhāśaya; standard); and the like

pres. part. caus. a-√spṛś, m. inst. sg.

words.gloss: to be fixed, held in view; possibly 'avacāryam', to be applied

hindi: क्योंकि योनि, यकृत्, प्लीहा, आँतों, गर्भाशय आदि के बीच, उन्हें चोट न पहुँचाने वाले और न छुआने वाले के द्वारा शस्त्र निश्चित किया जाना चाहिए; और खींचकर ऊपर करना, नीचे खींचना, घुमाना, काटकर निकालना, काटना, चीरना, दबाना और सीधा करना एक हाथ से करने चाहिए।
english: Since, among the yoni, liver, spleen, intestines, womb (garbhāśaya) and the like, the instrument has to be fixed (avadhārya) by one who does not injure them and does not cause touching; and pulling up, pulling down, turning round, cutting out, cutting through, splitting, pressing and straightening are to be done with one hand.

text_flags.why: possible: 'avadhāryam' may be a misprint of 'avacāryam' (to be applied), cf. avacārayet in 112; dh/c confusion is plausible in this print

notes: Hard unit; confidence is medium to low. 'avadhāryam' (to be fixed, held in view) is printed; 'avacāryam' (to be applied; cf. avacārayet in 112) is a possible original, see flag. 'tān anupahiṃsatā asparśayatā' is read as 'by one who neither injures them nor lets (it, the instrument) touch (them)'; the object of 'asparśayatā' is not stated, so this is a reading. 'madhye' with the list: 'among'. The printed forms 'vyāvarttana', 'utkarttana' show the book-wide rtt spelling (normalised to rt); 'pīḍanarjūkaraṇāni' = pīḍana-ṛjūkaraṇāni (a+ṛ gives ar). The eight operations are listed as neuter nouns with 'kāryāṇi'; 'ekena pāṇinā' = with one hand. Continues from 102 (the reason: GROUPING appears to continue 102).
lines_deva: यतो योनियकृत्प्लीहान्त्रगर्भाशयादीनां मध्ये ताननुपहिंसताऽस्पर्शयता शस्त्रमवधार्यमुत्कर्षणापकर्षणव्यावर्त्तनोत्कर्त्तनच्छेदनभेदनपीडनर्जूकरणानि चैकेन पाणिना कार्याणि
lines_iast: yato yoniyakṛtplīhāntragarbhāśayādīnāṃ madhye tānanupahiṃsatā'sparśayatā śastramavadhāryamutkarṣaṇāpakarṣaṇavyāvarttanotkarttanacchedanabhedanapīḍanarjūkaraṇāni caikena pāṇinā kāryāṇi

words.gram: m. acc. sg. used as adj.

hindi: इसलिए ईश्वर यानी स्वामी से पूछकर और परम प्रयत्न का सहारा लेकर, उसे जानने वालों के साथ उसका उपक्रम करे।
english: Therefore, having consulted the īśvara (lord), and having resorted to supreme effort, accompanied by those who know it, one should undertake it.
notes: īśvara = lord, master (here probably a ruler or head of the household; not defined, so left as 'lord'); not the divine. 'tadvidya' is taken as those who know that (the craft). 'tam' (masculine) is rendered 'it'; the referent is not named (the case or the fetus; unclear). 'paraṃ' is taken with 'yatnam' (supreme effort); the printed 'yatnamāsthāyatadvidyasahitastamupakramet' runs words together, split here without a flag.

words.gloss: in non-action, if no action is taken

hindi: कर्म न करने पर मृत्यु निश्चित है।
english: In inaction, death is certain.
notes: Copula understood. The subject (mother or the woman) is not stated.

words.gloss: udara (a disease of the belly, probably ascites-type); aśmarī (urinary stone; standard); and so on

hindi: वैसे ही उदर यानी पेट के रोग, सम्भवतः जलोदर की प्रकृति के, अश्मरी यानी पथरी आदि का भी।
english: Likewise also of udara (a belly disease, probably ascites-type), aśmarī (urinary stone) and so on.

text_flags.why: possible: the genitive plural 'prabhṛtīnām' has lost its anusvara before api

notes: Elliptical: no verb; what is said of them (that surgery is needed, or that death follows inaction) is not stated and is not supplied. Printed 'prabhṛtīnāpi' lacks the anusvara of prabhṛtīnām (see flag). udara here is the disease (belly disease, probably ascites-type: probable) beside aśmarī; elsewhere in the book it can mean the belly. GROUPING: appears to continue 105.

words.gloss: cloth; pad (cumbhala); raised; hip, waist; region
śālmalī (silk-cotton tree, Bombax ceiba; standard); picchā (gum, slime; probable)

hindi: फिर उत्तान यानी चित लेटी हुई, मुड़ी जाँघों वाली और वस्त्र के चुम्भल यानी सम्भवतः गद्दी से उठाए गए कटि-प्रदेश वाली स्त्री के लिए, धन्वनागमृत्तिका, जिसका अर्थ अस्पष्ट है, शाल्मली-पिच्छा यानी सम्भवतः सेमल के गोंद और घी से हाथ और योनि को चुपड़कर गर्भ को निकाले।
english: Then, in the case of her who lies face up, with the thighs bent and the hip region raised by a cloth cumbhala (probably a pad), having anointed the hand and the yoni with dhanvanāgamṛttikā (unclear), śālmalī-picchā (probably the gum of the silk-cotton tree, Bombax ceiba) and ghee (ghṛta), one should extract the fetus (garbha).
notes: dhanvanāgamṛttikā is kept as printed and unsplit: it may hide mṛttikā (clay, earth) with a preceding word, but the division is not safe, so it is left unclear. śālmalī = silk-cotton tree, Bombax ceiba (standard); picchā in 'śālmalī-picchā' = its gum (probable), as elsewhere in the book. 'cumbhala' (printed cuṃbhala) is taken as a pad or roll (probably a variant of cumbala/cumbaka; probable). Genitives 'uttānāyāḥ…' stand loosely ('in the case of'). The printed 'athottānāyā' etc. are regular sandhi. The anointing is of the hand and the yoni (the objects of abhyajya).
lines_deva: अथोत्तानाया व्याभुग्नसक्थ्या वस्त्रचुंभलोन्नमितकटिप्रदेशायाश्च धन्वनागमृत्तिकाशाल्मलीपिच्छाघृतैरभ्यज्य हस्तं योनिंच गर्भमाहरेत्
lines_iast: athottānāyā vyābhugnasakthyā vastracuṃbhalonnamitakaṭipradeśāyāśca dhanvanāgamṛttikāśālmalīpicchāghṛtairabhyajya hastaṃ yoniṃca garbhamāharet

words.gloss: because of following the natural direction (ānulomya)

hindi: वहाँ दोनों जाँघों से आए हुए का, आनुलोम्य यानी स्वाभाविक दिशा में होने के कारण, केवल कटा हुआ।
english: There, of one who has come by the two thighs, because of ānulomya (following the natural direction), only cut (chinna).
notes: The sense is uncertain and the unit is elliptical (no verb or noun for what is cut or to be cut is given and none is supplied); 'chinnam eva' may mean that only cutting is done, or may be a corrupt reading (an alternative such as 'achinnam' is not adopted). 'sakthibhyām āgata' is taken as presenting by the two thighs; the printed run-together 'sakthibhyāmāgatasyānulomyācchinnameva' is split without a flag (regular sandhi). Not enriched.
