words.gram: tat-puruṣa, n. acc. sg. used as ind.

words.gloss: of the one who has entered, presented

hindi: जिसकी एक जाँघ आगे आई हो उसकी दूसरी जाँघ को फैलाकर; जो नितम्ब-प्रदेश से आया हो उसके नितम्ब-प्रदेश को दबाकर ऊपर उठाकर और दोनों जाँघों को फैलाकर; जो तिरछा आया हो घुमाकर, या पिछले आधे भाग को उठाकर अगले आधे भाग को सीधा करके सन्तान के मार्ग में लाकर; जिसका सिर बगल की ओर घूमा हो उसके कन्धे को दबाकर ऊपर उठाकर सिर को सन्तान के मार्ग में लाकर; जिसकी दोनों भुजाएँ आगे आई हों उसके दोनों कन्धों को ऊपर की ओर दबाकर सिर की जड़ को लाकर निकाले।
english: For one who has presented with one thigh, having stretched out the other thigh; for one who has come at the buttock region, having pressed down the buttock region and lifted upward, having stretched out the two thighs; for one who has come transversely, having turned round, or having lifted the hind half and brought the front half to the path of the offspring straight; for one whose head is turned to the side, having pressed the shoulder and lifted upward, having brought the head to the path of the offspring; for one who has presented both arms, having pressed the two shoulders upward and brought the base of the head, one should draw out.

text_flags.why: possible: the dual of sakthi (neuter) is sakthinī; 'sakthyanī' has an extra y
possible: the absolutive is prasārya; the final e looks like a print slip
possible: 'parādarddham' has an extra da; aparārdha (hind half) is intended, in contrast to pūrvārdha (front half)

notes: One sentence with a series of cases; the one verb 'nirharet' (should draw out) closes it, and no object is stated. Each case begins with a genitive 'for one who…'; the 'one' is the fetus by context only. 'apatyapatha' = path of the offspring, probably the birth passage (probable). 'pratyārjavam' is taken as 'toward straightness' and may be a different word; the sense 'straight' is plain. In 'śirasoṃ'saṃ' and 'utpīḍyāṃ'sau' the printed apostrophe is a print habit before aṃsa; no flag. The rdd spelling in 'parādarddham/pūrvārddham' is the book-wide normalisation to rd. 'sphigdeśa' is the buttock region (sphik/sphij). The sense of the lifting is as printed ('ūrdhvam utkṣipya'); the text does not say what is lifted beyond the object named. Modern equivalents (probable, not stated by the text): the cases look like one leg presenting, breech (sphik-deśa), transverse lie (tiryak), head turned aside, and both arms presenting.
lines_deva: एकस्मिन् सक्थ्नि प्रपन्नस्येतरं सक्थि प्रसार्य स्फिग्देशागतस्य स्फिग्देशंप्रनिपीड्योर्ध्वमुत्क्षिप्य सक्थ्यनी प्रसार्ये तिर्यगागतस्य परिवर्त्य वाऽपरादर्द्धमुत्क्षिप्य पूर्वार्द्धमपत्यपथं प्रत्यार्जवमानीय पार्श्ववृत्तशिरसोंऽसं प्रतिपीड्योर्ध्वमुत्क्षिप्य शिरोऽपत्यपथमानीय बाहुद्वयं प्रपन्नस्योर्ध्वमुत्पीड्यांऽसौ शिरोमूलमानीय निर्हरेत्
lines_iast: ekasmin sakthni prapannasyetaraṃ sakthi prasārya sphigdeśāgatasya sphigdeśaṃpranipīḍyordhvamutkṣipya sakthyanī prasārye tiryagāgatasya parivartya vā'parādarddhamutkṣipya pūrvārddhamapatyapathaṃ pratyārjavamānīya pārśvavṛttaśirasoṃ'saṃ pratipīḍyordhvamutkṣipya śiro'patyapathamānīya bāhudvayaṃ prapannasyordhvamutpīḍyāṃ'sau śiromūlamānīya nirharet

hindi: पर जो मुड़े हुए मध्य भाग वाला हाथ, पैर और सिर से योनि में आता है।
english: But the one who, with its middle bent, comes to the yoni with hands, feet and head.

text_flags.why: possible: 'abhyugna' is not a known word; abhugna (bent) is used in the next unit

notes: The relative clause is complete; its main clause is in 112 ('tau mūḍhau'), so the sentence continues over 110-112 (GROUPING: appears to continue into 111 and 112). 'pratipadyate' = enters/reaches; rendered 'comes to'. Printed 'abhyugna' is not a word; see flag (cf. abhugna in 111).

hindi: और जो मुड़ा हुआ ही एक पैर से योनि में और दूसरे से गुदा में।
english: And the one who, just bent, (comes) with one foot to the yoni, with the second to the anus (pāyu).
notes: Elliptical: the verb 'pratipadyate' is carried from 110 and is not supplied. pāyu = anus (standard). The printed 'yaścābhugnaevaikena' = yaḥ ca abhugnaḥ eva ekena (regular sandhi, hiatus). GROUPING: appears to continue 110.

hindi: वे दोनों मूढ़ हाथ से निकाले नहीं जा सकते, इसलिए शस्त्र का प्रयोग करे।
english: Those two, mūḍha, cannot be extracted by the hand; thus one should apply the instrument (śastra).
notes: 'iti' closes the reason ('thinking: they cannot be extracted by hand'); rendered with 'thus' and left out of any quotation. 'aśakyau' = not possible (to be) (inf. in passive sense). 'tau' = the two cases of 110 and 111; the text does not say so in so many words. Hindi 'मूढ़' keeps the technical sense (stuck); not enriched.

words.gloss: round; tip (maṇḍalāgra, a round-tipped knife; probable)

hindi: फिर स्त्री को आश्वस्त करके, मण्डलाग्र यानी सम्भवतः गोल नोक वाले शस्त्र या अंगुलिशस्त्र यानी सम्भवतः उँगली के शस्त्र से चीरकर, सिर की खोपड़ी के टुकड़े निकालकर, शंकु से ठोड़ी, तालु, छाती या काँख में पकड़कर हटा ले।
english: Then, having comforted the woman, having split open with a maṇḍalāgra (probably a round-tipped knife) or an aṅguliśastra (probably a finger-knife), having removed the pieces of the skull, having seized with a hook (śaṅku) at the chin, the palate, the chest or the armpit, one should draw (it) away.

text_flags.why: possible: 'tāluki' is not a form (tālu is neuter, loc. tāluni); ni misread as ki

notes: The objects of 'vidārya' and 'apaharet' are not stated (the head or the fetus by context); '(it)' is shown in brackets. 'tāluni urasi' replaces the printed 'tālukyurasi' (see flag). Whether the hook seizes at the chin, palate, chest or armpit, or the fetus is drawn from them, is not settled by the wording; the first is the plainer reading. maṇḍalāgra and aṅguliśastra are instrument names; the tags are probable. Printed 'athastriyamāśvāsya' joins atha and striyam (spacing).
lines_deva: अथस्त्रियमाश्वास्य मंडलाग्रेणांगुलिशस्त्रेण वा विदार्य शिरःकपालान्याहृत्य शंकुना गृहीत्वा चुबुके तालुक्युरसि कक्षायां वाऽपहरेत्
lines_iast: athastriyamāśvāsya maṃḍalāgreṇāṃguliśastreṇa vā vidārya śiraḥkapālānyāhṛtya śaṃkunā gṛhītvā cubuke tālukyurasi kakṣāyāṃ vā'paharet

words.gloss: eye; projection, rim (akṣikūṭa; probably the eye-socket rim; probable)

hindi: या जिसका सिर विदीर्ण न हुआ हो, अक्षिकूट यानी सम्भवतः आँख के गड्ढे के किनारे पर या गण्ड यानी गाल में।
english: Or one whose head is unsplit, at the akṣikūṭa (the eye-socket rim, probably) or at the cheek (gaṇḍa).
notes: Elliptical: no verb; the action (seizing with the hook, drawing away) is carried from 113 and not supplied. GROUPING: appears to continue 113. The unstated noun after 'abhinnaśirasam' is the fetus by context. akṣikūṭa = projection or rim of the eye region; the exact part is not firm. gaṇḍa = cheek (it can also mean temple).

hindi: वैसे ही कन्धे में अटके हुए का कन्धे के स्थान पर भुजा को काटकर; दृति यानी चमड़े की मशक की तरह फूले हुए का वायु से भरे पेट को चीरकर और आँतों को निकालकर, ढीले हुए को निकाले।
english: Likewise, for one stuck at the shoulder, having cut off the arm at the shoulder region; for one swollen like a skin-bag (dṛti), having split open the belly (udara) full of wind (vāta) and cast out the intestines, one should extract (it) when it has become slack.
notes: The objects of 'chittvā' etc. and of 'āharet' are not stated; '(it)' is shown in brackets. 'dṛteḥ iva ādhmātasya': dṛti = a skin or leather bag (a bellows or water-skin); the ablative is read as the case of comparison used loosely ('like'). 'vāta-pūrṇam' = full of wind (vāta, plain wind). The printed spelling 'chitvā' (single t) is a spelling variant of chittvā, recorded here once for the chunk (also in 119); no flag. Printed 'tathā'ṃsa…' shows the print habit of an avagraha before aṃsa.
lines_deva: तथाऽंससंसक्तस्यांसदेशे बाहुं छित्वा दृतेरिवाध्मातस्य वातपूर्णमुदरमवदार्य निरस्यांत्राणि शिथिलीभूतमाहरेत्
lines_iast: tathā'ṃsasaṃsaktasyāṃsadeśe bāhuṃ chitvā dṛterivādhmātasya vātapūrṇamudaramavadārya nirasyāṃtrāṇi śithilībhūtamāharet

hindi: जघन में अटके हुए का जघन की हड्डियों को तोड़कर।
english: For one stuck at the hips (jaghana), having broken the hip bones (jaghana-kapāla).

text_flags.why: possible: 'śakta' (able) does not fit; sakta (stuck) matches aṃsa-saṃsakta in 115

notes: Elliptical: the verb 'should extract' is carried from 115 and not supplied. kapāla = plate or bone (as in the skull-pieces of 113); jaghana-kapāla = the bones of the hip region (probably the pelvic bones; probable). The closing 'iti' ends the list of cases (kept out of the translation). Printed 'śakta' is read as 'sakta' (stuck), see flag. GROUPING: appears to continue 115.

hindi: और इस विषय में ये हैं।
english: And on this there are (verses).
notes: A formula introducing the verses that follow. 'verses' is the usual understood noun and is shown in brackets; it is not in the Sanskrit. The printed 'cātra' = ca atra.

hindi: गर्भ का जो-जो अंग वायु के वश अटक जाए, खण्ड-खण्ड। उस-उस को काटकर भली प्रकार निकाले, और माता को चोट से बचाए।
english: Whatever limb of the fetus (garbha) may get stuck by the power of wind (vāyu), piecemeal. Having cut that and that, one should remove it properly, and protect the mother from injury.
notes: [02.04.118] 'khaṇḍaśaḥ' (in pieces) most likely belongs with the cutting in 119 ('having cut it piece by piece'); here it is given at the end as printed. The relative clause is completed by 119 (GROUPING: appears to continue into 119). Printed 'yadyadvāyuvaśādaṃgaṃ' = yat yat vāyu-vaśāt aṅgam; 'vāyu' is plain wind here. [02.04.119] Printed 'tattacchitvā' = tat tat chittvā (chitvā spelling variant, see 115). The printed 'haretsamyagrakṣejjananīṃ' = haret samyak rakṣet jananīm. 'tat tat' repeats the relative 'yat yat' of 118 ('each such'). Continues 118.

words.gram: pres. part. a-√pat, f. acc. sg.

hindi: फिर न गिरती हुई अपरा यानी जेर को वैद्य पहले की तरह गिराए। इस प्रकार जिसका शल्य निकाल दिया गया हो, उसे गरम जल से सींचे।
english: Then the physician should cause the aparā (placenta) that is not falling to fall, as before. Thus one should sprinkle with warm water her from whom the śalya (dart, foreign body) has been drawn out.
notes: [02.04.120] aparā = placenta, afterbirth (standard). 'as before' (pūrvavat) points to an earlier procedure, probably the one for the afterbirth in 99 or earlier units; the unit does not say which. Printed 'athāpataṃtīmaparāṃ' = atha apatantīm aparām (regular sandhi). [02.04.121] Follows the removal of the retained placenta in units 119-120. Śalya (literally a dart) is not defined in the line; the context suggests the retained fetus or placenta, but the text does not say so. The woman is the understood object (feminine accusative nirhṛtaśalyām).

words.gram: adj. nom. sg. (masculine form beside feminine yoniḥ)

hindi: तब जिसके शरीर पर अभ्यंग किया जा चुका हो, उसे योनि में स्नेह यानी तेल या वसा का पिचु यानी फाहा दे। उससे योनि मृदु हो जाती है और इसकी पीड़ा शान्त होती है।
english: Then one should give, to her whose body has been anointed, a swab (picu) of sneha (oil or fat) in the yoni (vagina). By that the yoni (vagina) becomes soft, and her pain subsides.
notes: [02.04.122] The printed snehapicuṃtataḥ is one token: sneha-picum tataḥ. Picu = a swab or pad (of cotton or wool); the material is not stated. Sneha = oil or fat (the kind is not stated). [02.04.123] mṛdu is grammatically masculine beside feminine yoni (adjective in a predicate; print and usage allow it). The optative bhavet is rendered as a plain statement of the result. "That" is the swab of unit 122.

words.gloss: rāsnā (Pluchea lanceolata or Alpinia galanga; disputed; on a conjectural reading of printed rāstrā)
the group of five called pañcakolaka (named in note)

hindi: दीप्यक यानी सम्भवतः अजवायन, अतिविषा यानी अतीस, अनुमानित पाठ पर रास्ना जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, हींग, इलायची और पंचकोलक यानी पाँच का समूह, जिसमें सामान्यतः पिप्पली, पिप्पलीमूल, चव्य, चित्रक और सोंठ गिने जाते हैं, पर यह पंक्ति उन्हें नाम से नहीं कहती। चूर्ण को स्नेह यानी तेल या वसा के साथ, या कल्क यानी लुगदी, या क्वाथ यानी काढ़ा, उसी प्रकार पिलाए।
english: Dīpyaka (probably ajwain), ativiṣā (atis), rāsnā (on a conjectural reading of the printed rāstrā; identity disputed), hiṅgu (asafoetida), elā (small cardamom) and the pañcakolakas (the group of five; usually pippalī, pippalīmūla, cavya, citraka and śuṇṭhī, though this line does not name them). One should make (her) drink the powder with sneha (oil or fat), or the kalka (paste), or the decoction (kvātha), likewise.

text_flags.why: possible: the drug name is rāsnā; stra for sna is a known confusion in this print (same word in 148)
possible: a stray space; hiṅgu + elā = hiṅgvelā, so the g of hiṅgu sits at the head of the next token
possible: kvātha (decoction) is meant; the v is missing (also in 130)

notes: [02.04.124] GROUPING: appears to continue in unit 125, where the verb (pāyayet) and the forms of administration are given; this unit is only the list of drugs (bare list forms, ending in the accusative plural pañcakolakān). The printed tokens hiṃ | gvelāpaṃcakolakān are hiṅgu + elā + pañcakolakān; the printed hiṃ is hiṅ- and the "gv" at the head of the second token completes hiṅgv- (hiṅgu + elā gives hiṅgvelā); the first token is given as hiṅgu whole. Identifications: dīpyaka = ajwain (probable; the older name is also given to other carminative seeds); ativiṣā standard; rāsnā disputed (one plant in north India, another in the south; see the gloss); hiṅgu standard; elā standard. Pañcakolaka is a group of five spices; the five are not named in this line (in the Aṣṭāṅga tradition usually pippalī, pippalīmūla, cavya, citraka and śuṇṭhī; probable, not stated here). The plural endings of a list ending in -ān are as printed. [02.04.125] The object is the drugs of unit 124 (not repeated here); that "her" is the woman is understood. pāyayet "should make (her) drink" (glossary: open wording). The text does not say which of powder, paste or decoction is preferred.
lines_deva: चूर्णं स्नेहेन कल्कं वा काथं वापाययेत्तथा
lines_iast: cūrṇaṃ snehena kalkaṃ vā kāthaṃ vāpāyayettathā

words.gloss: hiṅgu (asafoetida; on a conjectural reading of printed ghigu)
doṣa; flowing off; for the purpose of
words.gram: tat-puruṣa, n. acc. sg. used adverbially

hindi: कटुका यानी कुटकी, अतिविषा यानी अतीस, पाठा यानी सम्भवतः अकनादि, शाक यानी सम्भवतः सागौन की छाल, अनुमानित पाठ पर हींग और तेजनी जिसकी पहचान विवादित है। और उसी प्रकार दोष के बह निकलने के लिए और वेदना की शान्ति के लिए।
english: Kaṭukā (kutki), ativiṣā (atis), pāṭhā (probably velvetleaf), the bark of śāka (probably teak), hiṅgu (asafoetida, on a conjectural reading of the printed ghigu) and tejanī (identity disputed). And likewise, for the flowing off of the doṣa and for the relief of pain.

text_flags.why: possible: tvak + hiṅgu gives tvagghiṅgu; the printed ghigu has lost the nasal ṅ

notes: [02.04.126] Elliptical list; the verb (pāyayet, unit 125) is carried and not supplied. Compound division is partly ambiguous: śāka-tvak (bark of teak) is taken as one item; the alternative is śāka and tvak (a spice bark, probably cinnamon) as two items. Tejanī: candidates include tejovatī and other pungent plants; disputed. Kaṭukā standard. Pāṭhā: the identification given in the gloss is the usual one (probable); others are named by commentators. The compound ends in the accusative plural -īḥ as printed. [02.04.127] Gives the purpose of the drugs and forms in units 124-126. doṣasyaṃdārthaṃ is read doṣa-syanda-artham (the flow or discharge of the doṣa; doṣa not specified); the reading is not certain. "Likewise" (tadvat) refers to the way of giving described just before; the line has no verb.

hindi: इस प्रकार तीन रात, सात दिन; तब केवल स्नेह यानी तेल या वसा ही पिए। सायं अरिष्ट यानी खमीर उठाकर बनाया औषधीय पेय पिए, और उसी प्रकार भली-भाँति बनाया हुआ आसव यानी खमीर उठाकर बनाया औषधीय पेय।
english: Thus for three nights, for seven days; then she should drink sneha (oil or fat) alone. In the evening she should drink ariṣṭa (a fermented medicinal liquor), and likewise a well-made āsava (also a fermented medicinal liquor).
notes: [02.04.128] The wording "trirātram evam saptāham" gives two periods side by side with no "or" or "and"; whether they are alternatives (three nights or seven days) or successive is not settled by the line, so none is supplied. The subject (the woman) is understood. [02.04.129] The doubled k of sukkṛtam is a print habit (normalised in w, recorded here once for the chunk, as are the doubled consonants in vīryyojāṃsi, varddhaṃte, nivarttaṃte, kāśmaryya and arddha). The line does not say which ariṣṭa or āsava. Ariṣṭa and āsava are both fermented herbal preparations (standard).

words.gloss: śirīṣa (siris, Albizia lebbeck; standard); kakubha (arjuna, Terminalia arjuna; standard); decoction; swabs (picu)

hindi: और शिरीष यानी सिरस और ककुभ यानी अर्जुन के काढ़े के पिचु यानी फाहे योनि में रखे। और जो अन्य उपद्रव यानी जटिलताएँ हों, उनकी चिकित्सा अपने-अपने अनुसार करे।
english: And one should place in the yoni (vagina) swabs (picu) of the decoction of śirīṣa (siris) and kakubha (arjuna). And whatever other complications (upadrava) there may be, those one should treat each according to its own.

text_flags.why: possible: kvātha (decoction) with the v lost, as in unit 125

notes: [02.04.130] Picu as in unit 122 (swab). The compound can mean swabs soaked in the decoction or swabs of the decoction-drugs; the line gives no more. Kakubha = arjuna (standard). [02.04.131] Upadrava = a secondary affliction or complication. "Each according to its own" (yathāsvam): the noun to be supplied is not stated and none is added. Printed ye'nye is ye anye.

words.gloss: light; wholesome; little; eating (conjectural reading of printed padvyā)

hindi: अधिकतर वात को हरने वालों से पकाया हुआ दस दिन भोजन में हितकर है। और रस दस दिन; उसके बाद अनुमानित पाठ पर हल्का, पथ्य और अल्प भोजन करने वाली।
english: (What is) cooked mostly with Vāta-removing (ones) is beneficial in the meal for ten days. And the rasa (juice) for ten days; thereafter, on a conjectural reading, she who takes light, wholesome and little food.

text_flags.why: possible: prāyaḥ (for the most part) has lost its long ā; prayaḥ is not a word
possible: padvyā is not a word; pathyā (wholesome) fits the sense and the letters (th/d, y/v confusions occur in this print)

notes: [02.04.132] Copula "is" supplied; the nouns for "what is cooked" and for the Vāta-removing (ones) are not stated and are shown as (one)/(ones). Printed daśāṃhaṃ is daśa-aham ("for ten days"), accusative of duration. [02.04.133] The sentence has no main verb here; it reads as a continuation of unit 132 (diet of the woman). Rasa is the word as printed (juice or essence; the kind, e.g. a meat soup, is not stated and is not supplied). Param can be "thereafter" or "excellent"; "thereafter" fits the ten-day periods. The compound laghu-pathya-alpa-bhojanā is on a conjectural reading as flagged; meaning "eating light, wholesome and small meals".
lines_deva: प्रयो वातहरैः सिद्धं दशांहं भोजने हितं
lines_iast: prayo vātaharaiḥ siddhaṃ daśāṃhaṃ bhojane hitaṃ

hindi: स्वेद यानी सेंक और अभ्यंग यानी तेल मालिश में लगी हुई वह बलातैल आदि स्नेहों यानी तेलों या वसाओं का सेवन करे। चार महीनों के बाद वह क्रम से और सुखद।
english: Intent on sweating (sveda) and anointing (abhyaṅga), she should resort to sneha (oils or fats) beginning with balā oil. After four months, she, gradually, and pleasant (ones).
notes: [02.04.134] The subject "she" comes from the feminine parā (the woman after the ten-day diet). Balātaila is described in unit 137. [02.04.135] Elliptical and incomplete: the verb (probably "she should resort to", bhajet from unit 134) is not supplied. sukhāni is an adjective for an unstated noun (neuter plural); it may be a damaged word (compare mukhāni) but nothing in the print marks it; read as printed. ūrdhvam + ablative is taken as "after four months" (open point in the glossary). GROUPING: appears to continue unit 134.
lines_deva: ऊर्ध्वं चतुर्भ्यो मासेभ्यः सा क्रमेण सुखानि च
lines_iast: ūrdhvaṃ caturbhyo māsebhyaḥ sā krameṇa sukhāni ca

words.gloss: balā (country mallow, Sida cordifolia; standard); oil

hindi: अब हम बला यानी बरियार के तैल, बलातैल, का उपदेश करेंगे।
english: Now we shall teach the oil of balā (country mallow), balātaila.
notes: Opening formula of the recipe in unit 137. Balā = country mallow (standard; the Sida species are also used under this name).

words.gloss: yava (barley, Hordeum vulgare); kola (jujube, Ziziphus jujuba); kulattha (horse gram, Macrotyloma uniflorum); daśamūla (the ten roots); decoction
unclear (printed form; ends in tailasya, "of oil")
kākolī (identity disputed: Roscoea purpurea or a Fritillaria type)
kṣīrakākolī (identity disputed: Fritillaria roylei or Lilium polyphyllum)
aśvagandhā (ashwagandha, Withania somnifera; standard; on a conjectural reading of printed ahvagandhā)
śatapuṣpā (dill, Anethum sowa, or fennel, Foeniculum vulgare; disputed)
patra (leaf; probably Indian bay leaf, Cinnamomum tamala; probable)
tvak (bark; probably cinnamon, Cinnamomum verum; probable)
sarja (probably the sal tree, Shorea robusta, or its resin; probable)

hindi: बला की जड़ के काढ़े के छह भाग, उतने ही दूध के, यव, कोल यानी बेर, कुलत्थ यानी कुलथी और दशमूल के काढ़े का एक भाग, और अनुमानित पाठ पर तेल का भाग, जिसकी मात्रा अस्पष्ट है; सबको अनुमानित पाठ पर एक साथ करके, और महीन चूर्ण काकोली, क्षीरकाकोली, जीवक, ऋषभक जिन चारों की पहचान विवादित है, मुद्गपर्णी यानी सम्भवतः जंगली मूँग, माषपर्णी यानी सम्भवतः जंगली उड़द, मेदा और महामेदा नामक द्रव्य जिनकी पहचान विवादित है, क्षीरशुक्ला जिसकी पहचान अज्ञात है, मधुक यानी सम्भवतः मुलेठी, देवदारु यानी देवदार, मंजिष्ठा यानी मजीठ, चन्दन, सारिवा यानी सम्भवतः अनन्तमूल, बला यानी बरियार, तगर जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, कुष्ठ यानी कूठ, शतावरी, अनुमानित पाठ पर अश्वगन्धा, पुनर्नवा यानी गदहपूर्णा, शतपुष्पा यानी सोआ या सौंफ जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, पत्र यानी सम्भवतः तेजपात, त्वक् यानी सम्भवतः दालचीनी, सर्ज यानी सम्भवतः साल, शैलेय यानी सम्भवतः छरीला, वचा यानी बच, अगुरु यानी अगर, अनुमानित पाठ पर कालानुसार्य जिसकी पहचान अज्ञात है, और सैन्धव यानी सेंधा नमक डालकर, धीरे-धीरे मृदु अग्नि पर तैयार करके अच्छे पात्र में भली-भाँति सुरक्षित रखे।
english: Six parts of the decoction (kaṣāya) of balā (country mallow) roots, just as many (parts) of milk, a part of the decoction of yava (barley), kola (jujube), kulattha (horse gram) and the ten roots (daśamūla), and, on a conjectural reading, a part of oil whose measure is unclear; having put all that together (on a conjectural reading), and having added the fine powders—kākolī, kṣīrakākolī, jīvaka, ṛṣabhaka (identities of these four disputed), mudgaparṇī (probably a wild mung plant), māṣaparṇī (probably a wild urad plant), medā (identity disputed), mahāmedā (identity disputed), kṣīraśuklā (unidentified), madhuka (probably licorice), devadāru (deodar), mañjiṣṭhā (Indian madder), candana (sandalwood), sārivā (probably Indian sarsaparilla), balā, tagara (identity disputed), kuṣṭha (costus), śatāvarī (wild asparagus), aśvagandhā (ashwagandha, on a conjectural reading of the printed ahvagandhā), punarnavā (hogweed), śatapuṣpā (identity disputed: dill or fennel), patra (leaf, probably Indian bay leaf), tvak (bark, probably cinnamon), sarja (probably sal), śaileya (probably stone-flower lichen), vacā (sweet flag), aguru (agarwood), kālānusārya (on a conjectural reading of the printed kālānusārthya; unidentified) and saindhava (rock salt)—and having prepared (it) slowly over a gentle fire, one should store (it) in a good vessel, well guarded.

notes: Recipe (balātaila). Quantities: six parts of balā-root decoction, as many of milk, then a part of the yava-kola-kulattha-daśamūla decoction, then a measure of oil that is unclear in this print; GROUPING: appears to complete the recipe announced in 136. The "bhāgo bhāgaścaiturdaśatailasya" stretch cannot be restored from the print; no measure is supplied and the translation marks it conjectural. aikaṣṭyaṃ: probable aikyam (together); the translation says so. The big dvandva: the neuter plural ending -āni is shared by all members; ślakṣṇacūrṇāni is taken with it (the list as fine powders); whether the powders are "of" each drug or the drugs themselves are the powders is the same in effect. Identifications (once for the chunk, tags as in the glosses): standard: devadāru, mañjiṣṭhā, candana, kuṣṭha, śatāvarī, aśvagandhā, punarnavā, vacā, aguru, saindhava, balā; probable: mudgaparṇī, māṣaparṇī, madhuka, sārivā, patra, tvak, sarja, śaileya; disputed: kākolī, kṣīrakākolī, jīvaka, ṛṣabhaka (these four are the aṣṭavarga drugs in later tradition; their group name is not given here), medā, mahāmedā, tagara, śatapuṣpā; unidentified: kṣīraśuklā, kālānusārya. Printed ahva-/arthya- readings are flagged. The avagraha in vacā'guru is a print habit (ā + a). Hindi मेदा always with नामक द्रव्य (glossary). Yava, kola, kulattha: yava barley (standard), kola jujube (standard), kulattha horse gram (standard).

hindi: यह तैलराज यानी तेलों का राजा, भगवान् धन्वन्तरि को मान्य, राजाओं, राजमात्रों जिस शब्द का अर्थ अस्पष्ट है, कृशों, सूतिकाओं यानी प्रसूताओं, शिशुओं, बीती आयु वालों, सुकुमारों, महाग्रहों से गृहीतों, दीर्घ रोग से क्षीण शरीर वालों, जिनके अंग मर्म में बिंधे, गिरे, आहत, टूटे और उखड़े हों उनके, और अनुमानित पाठ पर दैव उपघात, अभिशाप और मनोज्वर से घिरे हुओं के लिए पान, नावन यानी नाक में डालना, अभ्यंग और बस्ति यानी एनिमा में प्रयोग करने योग्य है।
english: This king of oils, approved by the venerable Dhanvantari, is to be used in drinking, nasal administration (nāvana), anointing and enema (basti) for kings, for rājamātras (a term of unclear sense), for the emaciated, for women recently delivered (sūtikā), for infants, for those past age, for the delicate, for those seized by great graha (seizers), for those whose bodies are wasted by long illness, for those whose limbs are pierced at a marma (vital spot), fallen, struck, broken and dislocated, and, on a conjectural reading, for those afflicted by divine injury, by cursing and by mind-fever (manojvara).

text_flags.why: possible: mamo is probably mano (m/n confusion). daivāepaghāta is the Devanagari o-matra printed as ā + e (दैवाेपघात = daivopaghāta), a typographic split rather than damage; the conjecture lies in mamo -> mano.

notes: Dhanvantari is named as the authority; taila-rāja "king of oils" is the recipe of 137 (balātaila). "Rājamātra" is not clearly known (kingly persons, royal kin or an official class have all been suggested; none is certain) and is not translated further. "Atītavayasām" = "of those whose age has gone by", taken as the aged; "past age" is kept literal. "Mahāgrahagṛhīta" = seized by great graha; graha = seizing (seizer), not "seizure". The compound marmaviddha-…-aṅga can also be read as "those pierced at marma, fallen, struck, broken, and those with dislocated limbs"; the division is not fixed by the print. Printed eṣa before bh (visarga dropped by regular sandhi) and dhanvantarer abhi (r-sandhi) are regular. Nāvana = nasal administration (nasya); basti = enema here (the device or bladder sense is not intended).

hindi: उससे बल, पौरुष, स्मृति, मति, मेधा, अग्नि यानी पाचन अग्नि, वीर्य यानी शक्ति और ओज बढ़ते हैं, और पक्षाघात यानी अर्धांग का लकवा, आक्षेपक यानी ऐंठन के दौरे, अर्दित यानी चेहरे का लकवा आदि अनेक प्रकार के वात विकार, गुल्म यानी पेट की गाँठ, हिध्मा यानी हिचकी, श्वास यानी साँस की कठिनाई और कास यानी खाँसी दूर होते हैं।
english: By that, strength, manly vigour (pauruṣa), memory, understanding, intellect (medhā), digestive fire (agni), vīrya (potency) and ojas (vital essence) increase, and the various Vāta disorders beginning with pakṣaghāta (hemiplegia), ākṣepaka (convulsive disorder) and ardita (facial paralysis), gulma (abdominal lump), hidhmā (hiccup), śvāsa (breathlessness) and kāsa (cough), cease.
notes: Modern equivalents: pakṣaghāta = hemiplegia (standard); ākṣepaka = convulsive disorder (standard); ardita = facial paralysis of the Bell's palsy type (standard); gulma = abdominal lump or mass (standard; the exact modern entity is not fixed); hidhmā, śvāsa, kāsa standard. The last four are listed in the same clause; the text names them as ceasing in the same clause, it does not say they are Vāta disorders. Doubled consonants (vīryyojāṃsi, varddhaṃte, nivarttaṃte) are print habits. Doṣa Vāta is capitalised.

hindi: यदि बस्तिद्वार पर विपन्न हुई स्त्री की कुक्षि यानी पेट फड़के, जन्म के समय तब शीघ्र चीरकर शिशु को निकाले।
english: If the kukṣi (belly) of a woman who has perished at the bastidvāra (door of the basti) quivers, At the time of birth, then, quickly having split (it) open, one should take out the child.
notes: [02.04.143] GROUPING: the sentence is completed in unit 144. "Perished" (vipanna) means ruined or dead; the context (extracting the child) suggests death but the line does not say so. "Bastidvāra" is not explained in the line (the opening of the bladder region or the pelvic outlet are possible); read literally. Kukṣi = belly or abdomen, not specifically the womb. [02.04.144] GROUPING: appears to complete unit 143 (the main clause). The object of pāṭayitvā (the belly, kukṣi) is not stated and is shown as (it). Janmakāle can also be "at the proper time of birth".

hindi: मधुक यानी सम्भवतः मुलेठी, शाक यानी सम्भवतः सागौन का बीज, और पयस्या जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, सम्भवतः विदारीकन्द, और सुरदारु यानी सम्भवतः देवदार। अश्मन्तक जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, सम्भवतः आपटा, काले तिल, ताम्रवल्ली जिसकी पहचान अस्पष्ट है, और शतावरी।
english: Madhuka (probably licorice), the seed of śāka (probably teak), and payasyā (identity disputed; perhaps the Indian kudzu), and suradāru (probably deodar). Aśmantaka (identity disputed; perhaps the apta tree), black sesame seeds, tāmravallī (the copper-coloured creeper; identity unclear) and śatāvarī (wild asparagus).
notes: [02.04.145] Opens the series of seven combinations (145-151), each a half-verse, given with milk (152) in the seven months (153). Śāka may also mean a vegetable; "teak" is the usual identification in drug lists (probable). Madhuka = licorice (probable; the tree Madhuca is the other possible plant). Payasyā: disputed (vidārī and other milky climbers are named). Suradāru and devadāru are both deodar. The verb "should apply" is in unit 153. [02.04.146] Second combination. Aśmantaka: disputed (the apta tree or a fig). Tāmravallī: literally "copper creeper", no standard identification here (unidentified); a synonym of another climber is possible. Kṛṣṇatila = black sesame (standard).

english: Vṛkṣadanī (probably the mistletoe vandā), payasyā (identity disputed; perhaps the Indian kudzu), latā (a creeper; identity unclear) and sārivā together with utpala (probably blue water lily). Anantā (identity disputed; sometimes the same as sārivā), sārivā, rāsnā (on a conjectural reading of the printed rāstrā; identity disputed), padmā (lotus, or a plant so named; unclear) and madhuyaṣṭikā (licorice).

text_flags.why: possible: rāsnā is the drug name; stra for sna as in unit 124

notes: [02.04.147] Third combination. Printed sāribā is sārivā (b/v interchange in this print, recorded once; no flag). The division latā | sotpalasārivā is chosen; the alternative is latā sotpalā | sārivā ("latā with utpala, and sārivā"). Latā alone is a generic word for creeper and no identification is made. Utpala may also be a different lotus; blue water lily is the usual reading (probable). Printed vṛkṣadanī (short a): the usual spelling of the drug name is vṛkṣādanī (vṛkṣa-adanī); kept as printed, no emendation made. [02.04.148] Fourth combination. Anantā and sārivā are both listed, so they are taken as separate drugs here. Padmā: the lotus, or padmaka (a different plant) — unclear. Madhuyaṣṭikā = licorice (standard).

words.gloss: the two bṛhatīs (large and small nightshade, bṛhatī and kaṇṭakārī; probable)
madhuparṇikā (identity disputed; perhaps guḍūcī, Tinospora cordifolia, or gambhārī)

hindi: बृहतीद्वय यानी सम्भवतः बड़ी और छोटी कटेरी, काश्मर्य यानी गम्भारी, क्षीरी वृक्षों की शुंग यानी कोंपलों की छाल और घी। पृश्निपर्णी यानी पिठवन, बला यानी बरियार, शिग्रु यानी सहजन, श्वदंष्ट्रा यानी सम्भवतः गोखरू, और मधुपर्णिका जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, सम्भवतः गिलोय।
english: The two bṛhatīs (the large and small nightshade, probably), kāśmarya (gambhārī), the bark of the shoots (śuṅga) of milk-yielding trees (kṣīrin), and ghṛta (ghee). Pṛśniparṇī (pithvan), balā (country mallow), śigru (drumstick tree), śvadaṃṣṭrā (probably puncture-vine), and madhuparṇikā (identity disputed; perhaps giloy).
notes: [02.04.149] Fifth combination. Bṛhatī-dvaya = bṛhatī plus kaṇṭakārī (probable). Kṣīri-śuṅga-tvacaḥ is a compound that can be read "bark of the shoots of milk-yielding trees" (taken here) or as three separate items (milk-yielding trees, shoots, bark); the trees are not named here (later tradition names four figs; not stated). Kāśmarya = gambhārī (standard). Doubled y in kāśmaryya is a print habit. [02.04.150] Sixth combination. Pṛśniparṇī standard. Śvadaṃṣṭrā is usually gokṣura (puncture-vine; probable); kaṇṭakārī has also been called by this name. Madhuparṇikā is disputed (guḍūcī, gambhārī or others).

words.gloss: kaseru (a sedge tuber, Scirpus grossus; probable)

hindi: शृंगाटक यानी सिंघाड़ा, बिस यानी कमलनाल, द्राक्षा यानी अंगूर, कसेरु यानी सम्भवतः मोथा-कुल का कसेरू नामक कन्द, मधुक यानी सम्भवतः मुलेठी और सिता यानी सम्भवतः मिश्री। ये सभी योग दूध के साथ, जो आधे श्लोक पर समाप्त होते हैं।
english: Śṛṅgāṭaka (water chestnut), bisa (lotus stalk), drākṣā (grape), kaseru (probably the sedge tuber of that name), madhuka (probably licorice) and sitā (probably white sugar). All these combinations (yoga) with milk, those that end at a half-verse.
notes: [02.04.151] Seventh combination. Sitā literally "white"; sugar is the usual sense in lists (probable). Bisa = lotus rhizome or stalk (standard). [02.04.152] GROUPING: appears to continue in unit 153, which supplies the verb yojayet. "Ardhaślokasamāpana" = ending at (completed within) a half-verse: each combination fills one half-verse (145-151). The printed sarvaitān is sarvān etān.
lines_deva: शृंगाटकं बिसं द्राक्षा कसेरु मधुकं सिता
lines_iast: śṛṃgāṭakaṃ bisaṃ drākṣā kaseru madhukaṃ sitā

words.gloss: kapittha (wood-apple, Limonia acidissima; standard); bilva (bael, Aegle marmelos; standard); bṛhatī; paṭola (pointed gourd, Trichosanthes dioica; standard); ikṣu (sugarcane, Saccharum officinarum; standard); nidigdhikā (kaṇṭakārī, Solanum virginianum; standard)

hindi: क्रम से सात महीनों में गर्भ के बहने यानी सम्भवतः गर्भस्राव होने पर प्रयोग करे। कपित्थ यानी कैथ, बिल्व यानी बेल, बृहती यानी बड़ी कटेरी, पटोल यानी परवल, इक्षु यानी ईख और निदिग्धिका यानी कटेरी।
english: In sequence, in the seven months, when the fetus is flowing (probably miscarrying), one should apply (them). Kapittha (wood-apple), bilva (bael), bṛhatī (large nightshade), paṭola (pointed gourd), ikṣu (sugarcane) and nidigdhikā (kaṇṭakārī, the small nightshade).

text_flags.why: possible: the compound goes with mūlaiḥ in unit 155 (roots of the six); the printed final -n is not needed (16 syllables either way)

notes: [02.04.153] GROUPING: appears to complete units 145-152 (the verb for the combinations). "Garbhe sravati" is a locative absolute: with the fetus flowing, i.e. garbhasrāva (miscarriage; probable). The object "them" is the combinations of 152 and is shown as (them). Seven combinations match seven months. [02.04.154] GROUPING: appears to continue in unit 155 (mūlaiḥ śṛtam …). The printed accusative plural does not fit mūlaiḥ; the sense "with the roots of these" is read, so the final n is treated as a misprint (possible). Kapittha = wood-apple, bilva = bael (glossary). Bṛhatī and nidigdhikā are the large and small nightshades (standard).

words.gloss: sārivā; anantā (identity disputed); payasyā (identity disputed); madhuyaṣṭī (licorice)

hindi: जड़ों से उबाला हुआ दूध महीने में प्रयुक्त करे, और उसी प्रकार आठवें में। नवें में सारिवा, अनन्ता जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, पयस्या जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, सम्भवतः विदारीकन्द, और मधुयष्टि यानी मुलेठी के साथ।
english: One should use milk boiled with roots in the month, and likewise in the eighth. In the ninth, with sārivā, anantā (identity disputed), payasyā (identity disputed; perhaps the Indian kudzu) and madhuyaṣṭī (licorice).
notes: [02.04.155] GROUPING: appears to continue unit 154 (the roots of the plants listed there). "Māse" has no ordinal and so is unresolved: it may be a month whose number has dropped out, or "for a month". The print is 16 syllables as it stands, so no dropped word is shown by the metre. The avagraha printed in tathā'ṣṭame (ā + a) is a print habit. Kṣīraṃmāse is divided kṣīram māse. [02.04.156] Elliptical: the month noun (māse) and the verb are not stated; yojayet comes in unit 157 and is not supplied here. The milk is understood from 155 but not named in this line. The avagraha printed after ā (sārivā'naṃtā) is a print habit.

words.gloss: yaṣṭimadhuka (licorice); nāgara (dry ginger, Zingiber officinale; standard); amaradāru (deodar); with

hindi: दसवें महीने में पयस्या जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, सम्भवतः विदारीकन्द, उससे पकाया हुआ दूध प्रयुक्त करे। अथवा यष्टिमधुक यानी मुलेठी, नागर यानी सोंठ और अमरदारु यानी देवदार के साथ।
english: In the tenth month one should apply milk cooked with payasyā (identity disputed; perhaps the Indian kudzu). Or with yaṣṭimadhuka (licorice), nāgara (dry ginger) and amaradāru (deodar).
notes: [02.04.157] The verb yojayet also serves unit 156 (ninth month). "Siddha" = cooked (glossary). Payasyā: see unit 145. [02.04.158] GROUPING: appears to continue unit 157 (the tenth-month milk, cooked with these instead). Amaradāru and devadāru are both deodar (standard). Nāgara = dry ginger (standard).

hindi: इस प्रकार गर्भव्यापत् नामक चौथा अध्याय।
english: Thus the fourth chapter, named Garbhavyāpat (mishap of the fetus).
notes: Colophon. Printed garbhavyāpannāma = garbhavyāpat + nāma (t + n gives n; regular sandhi). Garbhavyāpat: "mishap, calamity (vyāpad) of the fetus (garbha)". The printed caturtho'dhyāyaḥ is caturthaḥ adhyāyaḥ.
